sections.heading: Understanding the CG PET 2026 Final Answer Key

content.text: The final answer key is the officially validated set of correct answers published by CG Vyapam after reviewing all candidate objections raised against the provisional key. Here is what candidates need to know about it.

sections.heading: What Is the Difference Between Provisional and Final Answer Key?

items: The provisional answer key is released shortly after the exam and is open for challenges.
Candidates can raise objections - called "Dava Aapatti" - by paying a fee of ₹50 per challenge.
After reviewing all objections, CG Vyapam releases the final answer key, which is the authoritative version.
The final answer key is directly used to calculate every candidate's score and prepare the merit list.
No further objections are accepted against the final answer key.

sections.heading: What If a Question Is Found Incorrect?

content.text: If any question in the CG PET 2026 paper is found to be incorrect or dropped after the objection review process, all candidates are awarded marks for that question regardless of their response. In the 2025 edition, for example, four questions were dropped by the board and marks were awarded to all candidates.

sections.heading: No Negative Marking in CG PET

content.text: A significant advantage of the CG PET examination pattern is that there is no negative marking for incorrect or unattempted answers. Each correct answer carries marks based on the official key.

sections.heading: How to Check CG PET 2026 Result and Download Scorecard

content.text: Checking the CG PET 2026 result is a straightforward online process. Follow the step-by-step guide below to access your scorecard without any confusion.

Navigate to the "Results" or "CG PET 2026 Result" link on the homepage.
Log in using your Vyapam profile credentials (Registration Number and Date of Birth).
Your CG PET 2026 result and scorecard will appear on the screen.
Download and save the scorecard - it is mandatory for the counselling and admission process.
Take a printout for future reference.

sections.heading: After the Result: CG PET 2026 Counselling Process

content.text: Clearing the CG PET 2026 exam is only the first step. The actual seat allotment happens through the counselling process conducted by the Directorate of Technical Education (DTE), Chhattisgarh. Here is a complete overview of what comes next.

sections.heading: Overview of Counselling Rounds

content.text: CG PET counselling is typically held in 3 to 4 rounds, including spot rounds, scheduled from June to August 2026. Two separate phases of counselling are conducted:

items: Phase 1 - For Government and Government-Aided Colleges
Phase 2 - For Private Colleges

sections.heading: Step-by-Step Counselling Process

items: Counselling Registration - Register on the DTE Chhattisgarh counselling portal (separate from the CG Vyapam exam portal).
Choice Filling - Select your preferred colleges and courses in order of preference.
Seat Allotment - Seats are allotted based on CG PET rank, category, and choices filled.
Document Verification - Report to the allotted college or designated centre for document verification.
Reporting and Admission - Report to the allotted institute and complete the admission formalities.

content.text: Important: Missing the counselling registration deadline means losing your seat even if your rank is strong. Act promptly once the result is declared.

sections.heading: Documents Required for CG PET Counselling

content.text: Ensure all the following documents are self-attested and ready before counselling registration opens:

items: CG PET 2026 Scorecard / Rank Card
Class 10th and 12th Mark Sheets and Passing Certificates
Category Certificate (OBC/SC/ST, if applicable)
Domicile Certificate (mandatory for Chhattisgarh state quota seats)
Transfer Certificate (TC) from the last attended institution
Character Certificate
Passport-size Photographs
Photo ID Proof (Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, etc.)
Disability Certificate (if applicable)

sections.heading: Who Can Apply for Admission via CG PET 2026?

content.text: The CG PET 2026 serves students from Chhattisgarh as well as candidates from other states. Notably, candidates from other states can also apply for admission through JEE Main scores as an alternative pathway. Chhattisgarh domicile holders are eligible for the state quota seats during counselling.

sections.heading: Re-Evaluation Policy: Can You Challenge the Result?

content.text: A common question among candidates is whether re-evaluation of the answer sheet is possible. CG Vyapam evaluates all OMR answer sheets through a machine-based automated process aligned with the final answer key. Due to this, re-evaluation of the OMR sheet is not provided. However, candidates are encouraged to challenge any incorrect answer during the provisional answer key objection window (Dava Aapatti), which is the only official avenue for raising concerns before the result is finalised.

content.text: ICSE Class 10 Economics Syllabus 2026-27 covers six major units for students preparing for the ICSE 2027 board examination. The syllabus includes The Productive Mechanism, Theory of Demand and Supply, Market, Banking in India, Inflation and Consumer Awareness. The Economics examination carries 80 marks in theory and 20 marks in internal assessment, with a two-hour written paper.

Students should prepare the complete chapter-wise syllabus, including important economic concepts, demand and supply curves, banking functions, inflation and consumer rights. The Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations (CISCE) publishes its official syllabuses through cisce.org. Candidates should select the syllabus labelled Examination Year 2027.

sections.heading: ICSE Class 10 Economics Syllabus 2026-27 Chapter-Wise

content.text: The Economics syllabus for the ICSE Class 10 examination covers six major units. Each unit contains several concepts and subtopics that students should prepare.

rows: Land, Labour, Capital, Entrepreneur and Factors of Production
Demand, Supply, Curves, Laws, Elasticity and Determinants
Perfect Competition, Monopoly, Monopolistic Competition and Oligopoly
Money, Commercial Banks, Central Bank, Monetary Policy and Public Finance
Stages, Types, Causes and Effects of Inflation
Consumer Rights, Consumer Protection, RTI, PDS and Quality Certification

sections.heading: Unit 1: The Productive Mechanism

content.text: This unit introduces the four major factors of production and explains their contribution to economic activities.

sections.heading: Important Topics

items: Meaning and characteristics of land as a factor of production.
Productivity of land and factors affecting land productivity.
Meaning and characteristics of labour.
Division of labour, its types and advantages.
Efficiency of labour and reasons for low labour efficiency in India.
Meaning and characteristics of capital.
Physical and financial capital with examples.
Capital formation, its process and importance.
Meaning of entrepreneur.
Functions of an entrepreneur and contribution to economic development.

content.text: Students should understand the differences among land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship and explain how each contributes to production.

sections.heading: Unit 2: Theory of Demand and Supply

content.text: This unit examines how consumer demand and market supply are related to price and other economic factors.

sections.heading: Important Topics

items: Meaning and concept of demand and supply.
Types of demand.
Law of demand and law of supply.
Individual and market demand schedules.
Individual and market supply schedules.
Demand and supply curves.
Movement along demand and supply curves.
Shift in demand and supply curves.
Determinants of demand and supply.
Exceptions to the law of demand.
Meaning and types of elasticity of demand.
Meaning and types of elasticity of supply.
Percentage method of measuring price elasticity.
Factors affecting elasticity of demand and supply.

content.text: Students should practise drawing and interpreting demand and supply curves and clearly distinguish a movement along a curve from a shift of the entire curve.

Important: The accessible CISCE Economics syllabus reference specifies that numerical problems on elasticity are not for testing. Students should follow the corresponding instructions in their Examination Year 2027 document when preparing.

sections.heading: Unit 3: Market

content.text: The Market unit covers the meaning of a market and the different types of market structures.

rows: A Market with Many Buyers and Sellers
A Market with a Single Seller
Competition Among Sellers Offering Differentiated Products
A Market Dominated by a Small Number of Sellers

sections.heading: Unit 4: Banking in India

content.text: Banking in India is a broad unit that includes money, commercial banks, central banking, monetary policy and public finance.

sections.heading: Money

items: Barter system and its limitations.
Evolution and legal meaning of money.
Money as a medium of exchange.
Money as a measure of value.
Money as a store of value.
Money as a standard of deferred payment.

sections.heading: Commercial Banks

items: Meaning and functions of commercial banks.
Types of bank deposits.
Types of loans and methods of advancing loans.
Basic process of credit creation.
Primary and derivative deposits.

sections.heading: Central Bank and Monetary Policy

items: Meaning and functions of the central bank.
Issue of currency notes.
Banker's bank and lender of last resort.
Banker, agent and adviser to the government.
Custodian of foreign exchange.
Qualitative credit control methods, including moral suasion, margin requirements and credit rationing.
Quantitative credit control methods, including Bank Rate, Open Market Operations, Cash Reserve Ratio and Statutory Liquidity Ratio.
Basic understanding of demonetisation.

sections.heading: Public Finance

items: Meaning of public finance.
Sources of public revenue.
Direct and indirect taxes and their differences.
Meaning and objectives of Goods and Services Tax (GST).
Progressive, proportional, regressive and degressive taxes.
Non-tax revenue with examples.
Public expenditure and its classification.
Revenue expenditure and capital expenditure.
Reasons for increasing public expenditure.
Meaning and types of public debt.

content.text: Students should particularly practise comparison questions covering commercial banks and central banks, qualitative and quantitative credit controls, and direct and indirect taxation.

sections.heading: Unit 5: Inflation

content.text: This unit focuses on the meaning, categories, causes and economic effects of inflation.

sections.heading: Important Topics

items: Meaning of inflation.
Creeping inflation.
Walking inflation.
Running inflation.
Hyperinflation.
Demand-pull inflation.
Cost-push inflation.
Causes of demand-pull and cost-push inflation.
Differences between the two main types of inflation.
Negative effects of inflation on production.
Effects of inflation on fixed-income earners and business-income groups.

content.text: Students should understand the differences among inflation types and explain their effects using simple examples.

sections.heading: Unit 6: Consumer Awareness

content.text: The final unit deals with consumer exploitation, rights, duties and protection mechanisms.

sections.heading: Important Topics

items: Meaning of consumer exploitation.
Forms and reasons for consumer exploitation.
Meaning and importance of consumer awareness.
Consumer rights and consumer duties.
Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
Right to Information (RTI).
Food adulteration and its harmful effects.
Public Distribution System (PDS).
Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS).
AGMARK certification.
ECOMARK certification.

content.text: Students should be able to explain how consumer rights, consumer protection laws and standardisation marks help protect buyers.

sections.heading: ICSE Class 10 Economics Exam Pattern 2027

content.text: The Economics examination combines a written theory paper with an internal project or assignment.

The official subject syllabus specifies the overall assessment division. Students should refer to the specimen question paper for the question format, section-wise choices and applicable marking instructions.

sections.heading: ICSE Class 10 Economics Chapter-Wise Marks Distribution

content.text: The syllabus establishes the six required units but does not provide a confirmed fixed marks allocation for each individual chapter.
Students should not assume that every unit carries equal marks or rely on unofficial chapter-wise weightage tables as guaranteed examination allocations.
Prepare all six units and use the official specimen papers and previous examination papers to understand the expected question format.

sections.heading: ICSE Class 10 Economics Internal Assessment 2026-27

content.text: Students must complete at least one Economics project or assignment prescribed by their teacher.
The internal assessment carries 20 marks. The subject teacher and an external examiner assess the project independently.

sections.heading: ICSE Class 10 Economics Project Topics

content.text: The published syllabus provides project and assignment examples related to factors of production, taxation and GST.

sections.heading: Project 1: Factors of Production

content.text: Visit a local industrial unit and study how land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship are combined in the production process.

sections.heading: Project 2: Survey on Taxes

content.text: Conduct a survey of 15 people in the neighbourhood to study the types of taxes they pay. Analyse which type of tax respondents find easier to pay and explain the conclusion.

sections.heading: Project 3: Impact of GST

content.text: Visit a nearby store and select five commonly purchased products. Examine the impact of GST on their prices or demand and discuss the benefits or implications for producers, consumers and the government.
The final project topic, submission format and assessment requirements should be confirmed with the school's Economics teacher.

sections.heading: How to Download ICSE Class 10 Economics Syllabus 2026-27?

items: Visit the official CISCE website at cisce.org.
Open the syllabus or regulations and syllabuses section.
Select the ICSE examination.
Choose the syllabus corresponding to Examination Year 2027.
Find Economics under the Group II subjects.
Open the Economics (64) syllabus document.
Verify that its cover or page headings refer to Examination Year 2027.
Download and save the PDF for examination preparation.

sections.heading: ICSE Class 10 Economics 2026-27 Preparation Tips

items: Begin preparation with the six units listed in the syllabus.
Learn important definitions and distinguish closely related economic concepts.
Practise demand and supply schedules and curves.
Prepare comparison tables for different market structures.
Understand banking functions, GST and monetary policy terminology.
Revise inflation types, their causes and effects.
Learn consumer rights, duties and important consumer protection measures.
Complete the Economics project according to the teacher's instructions.
Use official specimen and past examination papers for revision.
Revise the complete syllabus instead of relying on unverified chapter weightage.

sections.heading: AIAPGET Counselling 2026 Schedule Released

content.text: AACCC has issued the complete online counselling schedule for AYUSH postgraduate admissions for the academic year 2026-27.
The schedule contains the dates for registration, payment, choice filling, choice locking, seat allotment processing, result publication, institute reporting and verification of joined candidates.
The counselling process consists of three regular rounds followed by two stray vacancy rounds for remaining seats.

AIAPGET-qualified candidates should read the official information bulletin before registering because the fee requirements, security deposit rules, eligibility conditions and withdrawal penalties differ according to the counselling stage.

sections.heading: AIAPGET Counselling 2026 Round 1 Important Dates

content.text: The first round begins with verification of the tentative seat matrix on 24 and 25 October 2026.
All stated closing times follow AACCC server time. Candidates should complete registration and payment before their respective deadlines instead of waiting until the choice-locking deadline.

content.text: The last date for AACCC AIAPGET Round 1 registration is 1 November 2026 at 2 PM.

Candidates who complete their registration must pay the applicable non-refundable registration fee and refundable security deposit. The payment facility will remain available until 5 PM on 1 November.
The choice-filling window remains open until 11:55 PM on the same date, but this later deadline does not extend the registration window.

content.text: Round 2 registration will begin on 16 November 2026. Candidates participating in this round must complete the prescribed steps within the revised schedule.

Select the applicable counselling type.
Pay the non-refundable registration fee and refundable security deposit.
Complete the registration process and retain the confirmation information.
Fill college and course preferences during the choice-filling period.
Review and lock choices by 1 November 2026 at 11:55 PM.
Check the Round 1 seat allotment result on 3 November 2026.

content.text: AACCC permits only one counselling registration application per candidate. Multiple applications can lead to debarment or other action under the counselling rules.

sections.heading: AIAPGET Counselling 2026 Eligibility Criteria

content.text: Candidates seeking AACCC postgraduate counselling must have qualified in AIAPGET 2026 and satisfy the applicable academic and institutional admission conditions.
The counselling covers eligible MD/MS postgraduate programmes in Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani and Homoeopathy.
Admission is subject to the relevant entrance examination merit, qualifying degree, internship requirements, institutional eligibility and applicable regulatory provisions.
Final eligibility is verified by the allotted institution. Merely registering for counselling does not guarantee a postgraduate seat.

sections.heading: AIAPGET Counselling 2026 Courses and Participating Institutions

content.text: AACCC conducts centralised counselling for specified postgraduate AYUSH seats.

rows: Applicable Internal PG Institutional Quota Seats

sections.heading: AIAPGET Counselling 2026 Choice Filling and Locking

content.text: Round 1 choice filling begins on 27 October and ends on 1 November 2026 at 11:55 PM.
Choice locking will be available on 1 November from 2 PM to 11:55 PM.
Candidates should check the available college and course options, confirm the applicable fees and arrange preferences according to their actual admission choices.
Once choices are locked, AACCC does not allow candidates to modify them. Students should therefore review the college, course and preference order carefully.
Earlier-round choices do not automatically remain valid for all subsequent counselling rounds. Candidates must submit fresh choices where required under the counselling scheme.

sections.heading: AIAPGET Counselling 2026 Round 1 Seat Allotment Result

content.text: AACCC will process the first-round seat allotment on 2 November 2026 and publish the result on 3 November 2026.
The allotment will be determined according to the applicable candidate merit, eligibility, preferences, category and available seats.
Candidates who receive seats should download the individual allotment information through the official portal and complete the prescribed joining formalities between 4 and 13 November.

sections.heading: AIAPGET Counselling 2026 Reporting and Admission Confirmation

content.text: After seat allotment, eligible candidates must report to the allotted institution within the scheduled reporting period.
The college will verify the candidate's academic qualifications, examination result, internship and category-related documents, where applicable.
AACCC instructs students to obtain an online-generated provisional admission letter after completing physical reporting.
Admission confirmation and any subsequent relieving or withdrawal must be processed through the official AACCC system. Offline changes are not recognised under the counselling scheme.

sections.heading: Documents Required for AIAPGET Counselling 2026

content.text: Candidates should keep their original records ready for admission verification.

items: AIAPGET 2026 admit card and scorecard

Relevant academic marksheets
Internship completion certificate, where applicable
Professional registration certificate, as required
Proof of date of birth
Valid photo identity proof
Applicable category, EWS or PwBD certificates
Other certificates required by the allotted college or specific quota
Fee payment and admission-related documents

content.text: The final document checklist depends on the candidate's course, category and allotted institution. Students must follow the current official information bulletin and college-specific instructions.

sections.heading: AIAPGET Counselling 2026 Security Deposit Refund and Forfeiture Rules

content.text: The registration fee is non-refundable. The security deposit may be refunded after completion of the counselling process if the candidate satisfies the refund conditions.

AACCC states that security money can be forfeited if a candidate does not join an allotted seat in Round 2 or later rounds, withdraws contrary to the counselling rules, or fails to comply with prescribed conditions.

There is no free exit from an allotted Round 3 or stray vacancy seat under the specified rules. Withdrawal or non-joining can also make a candidate ineligible for further AYUSH postgraduate counselling.
Candidates should read the official forfeiture and eligibility rules before deciding not to join an allotted seat.

items: Round 1 registration begins on 26 October 2026.
Complete registration by 1 November at 2 PM and payment by 5 PM.
Fill and lock choices by 1 November at 11:55 PM.
Check the first seat allotment result on 3 November.
Report to the allotted institution between 4 and 13 November if a seat is received.
Read the counselling fee, security deposit and forfeiture rules before payment.
Use only the official AACCC website for registration, choice filling and admission updates.

content.text: Once ICAI activates the admit card link, candidates can download their CA Final November 2026 hall ticket through the official examination services portal. Follow these steps:

Find the admit card download link for the CA Final November 2026 examination.

Submit the details to access the admit card.

sections.heading: ICAI CA Final November 2026 Group-Wise Exam Dates
Important Instructions

items: Download only from the official portal. Log in at eservices.icai.org with your Self Service Portal credentials, then go to Exams and select the Final November 2026 admit card. ICAI releases the hall ticket online only, with no physical copy by post.
Carry a printout and photo ID. Take a printed A4 admit card and a valid government photo ID. You can’t enter the exam hall without the admit card.
Check every detail on it. Verify your name, photo, signature, exam centre, papers and group. If anything is wrong, contact ICAI immediately, because corrections take time.

Know the dates and timings. Group I is on November 2, 4 and 6, and Group II is on November 9, 11 and 13. Papers 1 to 5 run from 2 PM to 5 PM, and Paper 6 from 2 PM to 6 PM. Reach the centre well before the reporting time on the admit card.

If the admit card doesn’t show, check your eligibility. Eligibility holds, such as articleship status updates (due by October 10), can stop it from appearing. Resolve these with ICAI and keep checking icai.org for official notices.

sections.heading: How to Prepare for CBSE Class 11 Biology Examination 2026-27?

content.text: Students can plan their Biology preparation using the official chapter list and marks distribution.

items: Complete all 19 chapters prescribed in the Class XI theory syllabus.
Give sufficient revision time to Human Physiology, which carries 18 marks.
Study biological classification, cell structures and plant physiology using the prescribed NCERT textbook.
Practise biological diagrams and explanations relevant to the syllabus.
Review the topics specifically excluded from summative assessment.
Keep the practical record and project work up to date.
Prepare for experiments, slide identification, spotting and viva voce.
Use the official CBSE syllabus PDF to check the scope of each chapter.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: Marks split: Biology is assessed out of 100 marks, with 70 for theory and 30 for practical. The subject code is 044.

Unit-wise weightage: Diversity of Living Organisms carries 15 marks, Structural Organisation 10, Cell: Structure and Function 15, Plant Physiology 12 and Human Physiology 18. Human Physiology is the heaviest unit.

Practical (30 marks): This covers a major experiment (5), a minor experiment (4), slide preparation (5), spotting (7), practical record and viva (4) and project work (5). Keep your records and project file complete before the practical.

Question types: The paper is described as roughly 20% MCQ or assertion-reason, 20% case-based or competency-based, and 60% short and long answer questions with compulsory diagrams. One source lists a section-wise pattern totalling 80 marks, which doesn’t match the 70-mark theory paper, so rely on your school’s sample paper.

Dates and chapters: I found no official Class 11 Biology exam date, since your school conducts Class 11 exams. Some sources say the syllabus has 19 chapters while another says 22 chapters. Check the official CBSE syllabus PDF and your school’s notices for the final chapter list and date.

Candidates must carefully note the slot printed on the admit card and appear for the test only at that date and time.

Test centres are allotted based on the preferences filled in the BITSAT application form and the availability of seats at each centre. items: Mobile phones, smart watches, Bluetooth devices, earphones or any form of electronic gadget.

Books, notes, written slips and any other study material.

items: Reach the exam centre at least 60 minutes before the reporting time to complete security checks and registration.
Carry the admit card and photo ID in original; photocopies of ID may not be accepted.
Do not carry prohibited items to the exam lab; there may not be any facility for safe-keeping of personal belongings.
Follow the invigilator’s guidelines for logging in to the computer, navigating between questions and submitting the test.
Any kind of malpractice or misconduct can lead to cancellation of candidature and further disciplinary action.

items: Immediately contact the BITS admission office using the helpline number or email given in the information brochure.

Follow the instructions given by the authorities and complete any required correction process before the exam day.

content.text: Unable to Download BITSAT Admit Card 2026
If the website is not opening or the admit card is not downloading:

items: Check your internet connection and browser; try clearing cache or using a different browser/device.
Ensure that you are entering the correct application number and password/date of birth.

sections.heading: How to Apply for Gujarat NEET UG Counselling 2026 Round 2

items: Visit the official website, medadmgujarat.org.

Set a password (typically 6–12 alphanumeric characters) for future logins.
Review and confirm all entered details, since registration details generally cannot be edited after confirmation.
Print the Registration Details/Slip, selecting a preferred Help Centre along with an available date and time slot for document verification.
Visit the chosen Help Centre in person with original documents and self-attested photocopies to complete verification and collect the signed Registration Acknowledgement Slip.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

sections.heading: NMAT 2026 Important Dates
NMAT 2026 Exam Pattern

content.text: NMAT 2026 is a computer-adaptive test that continuously adjusts question difficulty based on a candidate's previous responses. The exam consists of 108 questions across three sections, to be completed within 120 minutes.

items: Negative Marking: None.
Section Weightage: Equal weightage is given to all sections.
Section Order: Candidates can choose their preferred order for attempting sections.
Attempts: Up to 2 retakes are allowed (3 attempts in total) to improve performance.
Test Centres: The exam will be conducted at 64 test centres across 59 cities in India.

sections.heading: How to Apply for NMAT 2026

content.text: NMAT 2026 applications are accepted only in online mode through the official GMAC website. Candidates can follow these steps to register:

items: Visit the official GMAC website at mba.com.
Click on the NMAT 2026 registration link available on the homepage.
A new page will open; enter the required registration details.
Once registration is complete, fill in the application form.
Make the payment of the applicable application fee.
Click submit and download the confirmation page.
Keep a hard copy of the confirmation page for future reference.

sections.heading: NMAT 2026 Important Instructions

items: Complete registration before the closing date of 10 October 2026.
Scheduling of the exam slot must be completed by 22 October 2026.
The exam will be delivered anytime within the window of 2 November 2026 to 20 December 2026, based on the candidate's chosen slot.
Retain the downloaded confirmation page/receipt after submitting the application.
Refer only to the official mba.com website for updates, as third-party sources may not reflect the latest changes.

sections.heading: Why Take the NMAT Exam

content.text: NMAT by GMAC offers a few structural advantages to candidates:

items: Score-Friendly Format: No negative marking and equal weightage across all three sections.
Flexible Attempt Strategy: Candidates can choose their section order and attempt the exam up to 3 times.
Fast Results: Instant score preview after the test, with the official scorecard available for download within 48 hours.
Wide Reach: Test centres are available across 59-70+ cities in India, giving candidates flexibility in choosing a convenient location and date.
Preparation Support: Official prep material, including the NMAT Official Guide and both free and paid practice exams, is made available to registered candidates.

The re-evaluation window is closed. One source puts the re-evaluation and re-checking application window at May 10 to 25, 2026. Don’t rely on that, because I didn’t see an official HPBOSE notice for it. Improvement exams count towards later merit. One source says a second opportunity examination was set for June 2026 for students wishing to improve their scores, and its results are considered for the final merit list and Class 11 admission. If you’re considering this for a future cycle, check the board’s current notices first.

sections.heading: HPBOSE D.El.Ed Counselling 2026: Seat-Allotment Procedure

content.text: As per the official prospectus, counselling works as follows:

items: HPBOSE prepares a merit list based purely on total marks scored in the CET (no interview is conducted).
Candidates are called for counselling strictly in order of merit, category-wise, as per the reservation roster.
The date, time and venue for each counselling round is announced only on the official HPBOSE website - no individual letters, faxes or phone calls are sent to candidates.
At counselling, eligibility is finally verified against original documents.

Seats are allotted according to the candidate's stated institution preference and the seats available at that candidate's turn. This preference can be exercised only once - once a seat is accepted, it is final, and the candidate cannot request a change of institution.
A candidate who accepts a seat in one round cannot participate in later rounds for re-allotment.
Unfilled or vacated seats are carried forward to the next round strictly by merit.
There is no migration allowed between institutions after admission - neither between DIETs nor between private colleges.

sections.heading: How to Apply / Register for HPBOSE D.El.Ed CET and Counselling

items: Visit the official HPBOSE website: hpbose.org.
Click on the "CET / Vacancy" section, then select the D.El.Ed (CET) 2026 link.
Register and fill in personal, educational, category and exam-centre preference details in capital letters exactly as per your Matriculation certificate.
Upload a scanned photograph (JPG, under 20 KB, 3.5 cm x 4.5 cm) and signature (JPG, under 15 KB, 3.5 cm x 1.5 cm).
Pay the application fee online via net banking, debit card or credit card.
Submit the declaration and download/print the confirmation page for your records.
After the result and merit list are announced, regularly check hpbose.org for your counselling call - no separate communication is sent by post or courier.
Attend counselling in person on the notified date with all original documents, and exercise your institution preference to get your seat allotted.

sections.heading: Important Instructions for Candidates

items: The information provided in the online application (name, date of birth, category, etc.) is treated as final and generally cannot be changed once the correction window closes.
No separate letter, fax, email or phone call is sent for any round of counselling - candidates must track hpbose.org themselves.
There is no job guarantee from the Government of Himachal Pradesh after completing the D.El.Ed course.
Attendance requirement during the two-year course is 90%, with a 50% relaxation available for pregnancy/maternity cases on the Principal DIET's recommendation.
All seats are reserved for bonafide residents of Himachal Pradesh.
Any dispute regarding the CET or counselling falls under the jurisdiction of Dharamshala courts.

sections.heading: What Is HPCET 2026 Counselling?

HPCET counselling is the centralised admission process conducted by HPTU, Hamirpur, for candidates who have qualified the Himachal Pradesh Common Entrance Test. Through this process, qualified candidates register online, fill their course and college preferences, and get seats allotted based on their rank, category, and seat availability. Fill in personal, academic, and category details in the counselling-cum-admission form.
Upload the required scanned documents and photograph as per specifications.
Pay the applicable counselling fee through net banking, debit card, or credit card.
Fill course and college preferences in order of priority from the available seat matrix.
Lock your choices before the deadline; unlocked choices may be auto-considered as locked once the window closes.
Submit the form and save/print the confirmation page for future reference.

The counselling fee for candidates who do not already hold an HPCET score is structured by category, as per HPTU's notified fee schedule:

items: Online Registration: Candidates register at himtu.ac.in and pay the counselling fee within the notified window.
Choice Filling: Candidates select course and college preferences from the published seat matrix, in order of priority.
Locking of Choices: Preferences must be locked before the deadline; any choices left unlocked may be treated as locked automatically.
Seat Allotment: Seats are allotted based on HPCET 2026 rank, category, preferences submitted, and seat availability.
Document Verification: Allotted candidates upload or present documents for verification.
Admission Fee Payment: Candidates confirm their allotted seat by paying the admission fee.
Reporting to Institute: Candidates report to the allotted institute with original documents within the specified timeline.
Multiple Rounds: HPTU conducts more than one round of counselling including a mop-up or stray vacancy round until seats are filled.

Candidates who fail to confirm admission by the deadline risk cancellation of their allotted seat. HPTU typically conducts multiple counselling rounds including a mop-up/stray vacancy round to fill any seats that remain vacant after the initial rounds.

sections.heading: What Is HP PAT 2026?

content.text: HP PAT, or the Himachal Pradesh Polytechnic Admission Test, is a state-level entrance examination conducted annually by the Himachal Pradesh Technical Education Board (HPTEB). The exam serves as the gateway for admission into Diploma Engineering programmes at Government and Private Polytechnic colleges across Himachal Pradesh.

The HP PAT 2026 exam was held on May 17, 2026, in a single shift from 10:00 AM to 1:00 PM, in offline (pen-and-paper) mode, lasting 3 hours. The marking scheme awards 4 marks for every correct answer and deducts 1 mark for every incorrect response. The total marks for the exam are 600.

sections.heading: HP PAT 2026 Merit List & Tie-Breaking Criteria

content.text: The HP PAT 2026 merit list is published alongside the result on hptechboard.com. It ranks all qualified candidates based on their total marks obtained in the entrance examination. Understanding how ties are resolved helps candidates know exactly where they stand.
In cases where two or more candidates score identical marks, the board applies a tie-breaking formula in the following order of priority:

items: Marks in Chemistry - The candidate with higher Chemistry marks ranks higher.
Marks in Physics - If Chemistry marks are also equal, Physics scores are compared.
Marks in Biology/Mathematics - The next tiebreaker if Physics scores are also tied.
Marks in English - Applied if the above three subjects also result in a tie.
Age - In case of a further tie, the older candidate is given the higher rank.

items: Online Registration for Counselling - Candidates must register on the official portal.
Updating Class 10 Marks - Candidates are required to update their Himachal Pradesh Board Class 10 marks.
Choice Filling - Select preferred institutes and diploma courses.
Document Verification - Verify academic certificates, category certificates, and other required documents.
Seat Allotment - Allotment is published round-wise based on rank, category, and choices.
Reporting to Institute - Candidates who accept their allotted seat must report to the respective polytechnic within the stipulated deadline.

sections.heading: How to Calculate Marks Using HPCET 2026 Answer Key

content.text: Once the tentative answer key is downloaded, candidates can estimate their HPCET 2026 score by applying the marking scheme to their responses. The marking scheme for each paper is given in the official HPCET 2026 information brochure, and candidates must follow that pattern only.
The general process is as follows:

items: Note down the total number of questions and marks per question for your paper as mentioned in the HPCET 2026 exam pattern.
For every correct answer that matches the option given in the answer key, add the full marks allotted per question.
For every wrong answer, deduct marks as per the negative marking specified in the brochure.
No marks are added or deducted for questions which were left unanswered.
After going through all questions, total your marks to get your approximate score in HPCET 2026 for that specific course.

content.text: For example, if a paper carries 100 questions with 2 marks each and 0.5 marks negative per wrong answer, and a candidate gets 70 questions correct and 20 wrong, the estimated score will be: Correct: 70 × 2 = 140 Wrong: 20 × 0.5 = 10 (to be deducted) Estimated score = 140 − 10 = 130
This calculated score is only indicative; the final result will be based on the University’s evaluation and the final answer key.

sections.heading: HPCET 2026 Answer Key Objection Process (Tentative)

Candidates are therefore advised to carefully read the instructions provided with the HPCET 2026 answer key notice on the official website.
Typically, the objection process includes the following steps:

items: Objections must be submitted within a specified time window after the release of the tentative answer key.
Candidates have to mention the question number, booklet code, the answer given in the provisional key and the answer they believe is correct, along with supporting proof from authentic sources.
There may be an objection fee per question, which can be refunded if the challenge is found valid, depending on University rules.

content.text: After the objection window is closed, expert committees examine all challenges. Based on their recommendations, HPTU may revise the answers and publish the final answer key. The result is then prepared strictly on the basis of this final key, and further objections are normally not entertained.

Basic Eligibility for HPCET 2026 (UG & PG)
The detailed eligibility criteria are provided in the HPCET 2026 information brochure, and candidates must strictly verify them before applying. However, in broad terms:

items: For B.Tech and B.Pharmacy: Candidates must have passed 10+2 or equivalent examination from a recognised board with the required combination of subjects and minimum aggregate marks stipulated by HPTU.
For MCA, MBA, MBA (T&HM), M.Sc Physics and M.Sc Environmental Sciences: Candidates should possess a relevant bachelor’s degree with the minimum percentage specified in the prospectus.

content.text: For precise eligibility (including subject combination, age limit and relaxation details), candidates should always refer to the official HPCET 2026 prospectus available on the University website.
HPCET 2026 Exam Pattern & Marking Scheme
HPCET is conducted in offline mode as a pen‑and‑paper OMR based test. The exam pattern varies slightly from course to course, but some common features are:

items: The question paper consists of objective type multiple-choice questions.
The medium of the question paper is generally English.

HPCET 2026 Cut Off and Merit List
Once the results are announced, the University releases course-wise and category-wise cut off marks or merit lists. These cut offs are determined based on several factors, such as:

items: Number of candidates appearing for the exam
Total seats available in a particular course
Difficulty level of the question paper
Previous year cut-off trends and reservation norms

content.text: Candidates securing marks equal to or above the notified cut off will be considered for counselling and further admission processes.
HPCET 2026 Counselling Process (Short Summary)
Eligible candidates who qualify as per the HPCET 2026 cut off must participate in the University’s counselling process. The broad steps in counselling generally include:

items: Online registration for counselling within the stipulated dates
Payment of counselling fee (if any)
Filling and locking choices of courses and colleges
Verification of documents at designated centres or online, as per the procedure
Seat allotment based on merit, preferences and reservation policy

content.text: After seat allotment, candidates must confirm their admission by reporting to the allotted institute within the prescribed time along with original documents and fees.

sections.heading: HPCET 2026 - Application Fee/ Entrance Test Fee

content.text: The application fee must be paid online during form submission. Fee once paid is non-refundable. In case of multiple payments against the same form, a refund can be requested via the fee refund form available on HPTU website (Examination → Download Forms → Examination/Reevaluation fee refund form); processing may take about one month.

sections.heading: How to Apply for HPCET 2026 - Step-by-Step Guide

content.text: Applications are accepted only in online mode via the HPTU official website. Follow the steps below carefully to fill the HPCET 2026 application form without errors:

items: Visit the official HPTU website www.himtu.ac.in and navigate to the HPCET 2026 application page. Click on One Time Registration (OTR) under the "Services" section.
Click "Register →" and then "As Student". New users must click "New User? Sign up for Citizen Login".
You will be redirected to the Him Access Portal. Choose the Aadhaar number option, provide eKYC consent, enter OTP, then provide your mobile number and email to generate a unique Him Access ID.
Login "As Student" using your Him Access ID / registered mobile number or other available option.
Update your profile in four tabs: Applicant Details, Contact Details, Qualifications (10th, 12th, graduation if applicable), and Upload Photo & Signature (JPG/JPEG/PNG, 60-100 KB).
Click "Complete Profile" → Logout → Login again → navigate to "Courses List".
Under UG/PG list, click "Apply" against your desired course or combined course option (e.g., B.Tech & B.Pharmacy both, MBA & MCA, etc.).
Fill the HPCET 2026 Application Form: select quota (AIQ / HPSQ / NRI / KM), category, minimum qualification, sub-category etc. Ensure all entries match your profile/qualification details.

Tick the declaration checkbox, then click "Save Draft". Check under "My Applications", use "Edit Application" if corrections are needed, then click "Submit Application". After submission, no further edits are allowed.
Note down the Application Number (format: HPCET26XXXXXX) displayed on screen. Go to "My Applications" → click "₹ Pay XXXX" → Proceed to Payment and complete the fee payment via the payment gateway.

After successful payment, download and print the application form PDF. If the PDF icon does not appear, click the payment button again to refresh payment status. If not generated within 2 working days, email: [email protected] with your Form Number, transaction ID, and payment screenshot.

sections.heading: Documents Required for HPCET 2026

content.text: Keep the following documents ready in digital format before starting the HPCET 2026 application form. All documents must be scanned clearly and in the prescribed format/size.

items: Recent passport-size photograph (JPG/JPEG/PNG, 60-100 KB)
Candidate's signature in prescribed format (JPG/JPEG/PNG, 60-100 KB)
Aadhaar Card (for Him Access Portal registration)
Class 10 (Matric) mark sheet and certificate
Class 12 (10+2) mark sheet and certificate
Graduation degree mark sheet (for PG course applicants - MCA, MBA, M.Sc.)
Caste/Category certificate - SC/ST/OBC/EWS (if applicable)
BPL certificate (if claiming BPL fee concession)
Valid photo ID proof (Aadhaar/Voter ID/Passport)

sections.heading: HPCET 2026 - Exam Pattern (Course-wise)

content.text: HPCET 2026 is conducted in offline (OMR-based) mode in English language. The exam pattern varies by course. There is negative marking in all courses. Refer to the course-wise patterns below:
1. B.Tech & B.Pharmacy (Allopathy) - Direct Entry
Duration: 3 Hours 15 Minutes | Marking: +4 for correct, −1 for wrong, 0 for unattempted. In Section B, if more than 30 questions are attempted, only the first 30 are evaluated.
2. B.Sc. (HM&CT) / BHMCT
Duration: 2 Hours | Marking: +1 for correct, −0.25 for wrong, 0 for unattempted.
3. MBA / MBA (T&HM) / MCA
Duration: 2 Hours | Marking: +4 for correct, −1 for wrong, 0 for unattempted.
4. M.Sc. Physics

rows: Mathematical Methods, Classical Mechanics & General Properties of Matter
Atomic & Molecular Physics, KTG & Thermodynamics, Solid State & Electronics

content.text: Duration: 2 Hours | Marking: +1 for correct, −0.25 for wrong, 0 for unattempted.
5. M.Sc. Environmental Sciences
Duration: 2 Hours | Marking: +1 for correct, −0.25 for wrong, 0 for unattempted.

sections.heading: HPCET 2026 - Result & Counselling

content.text: The HPCET 2026 Result is tentatively expected by 21 May 2026 on the official HPTU website. After result declaration, candidates will need to apply separately for centralized counselling using a new online form (Prospectus Part-II: Admission Brochure 2026-27) which will be released in May 2026.

Admission to all courses is made on the basis of merit (rank/marks) in HPCET 2026 or applicable National Level Entrance Tests, subject to fulfillment of minimum educational qualification. Centralized counselling is tentatively scheduled for June 2026 and classes are expected to start from the last week of July or first week of August 2026.

content.text: Exam centres for HPCET 2026 vary by course. The University may add, change, or cancel centres depending on the number of applicants. Candidates should select their preferred centre carefully during form submission; centre change requests (if approved) attract a fee of ₹2000.

content.text: The Health & Medical Education (H&ME) Department, Union Territory of Ladakh, issued revised guidelines on September 22, 2026, for admission to MBBS and BDS seats under the Central Pool. The revision replaces the existing category-wise roster system with a single merit list based purely on NEET ranking. The change was made following the creation of seven new districts in Ladakh and was approved by Lieutenant Governor V K Saxena. For the 2026-27 academic session, the Centre has allotted 7 MBBS seats and 2 BDS seats to Ladakh under the Central Pool.

sections.heading: Jharkhand GNM Round 2 Choice Filling: Step-by-Step Process

content.text: Candidates need to log in, select their preferred colleges, and lock their choices online. Here is the complete process:

items: Visit the official JCECEB GNM portal at gnm.jceceb.co.in.
Click on the link for "Online Counselling for GNM 2026".
Log in using your Application Number/Roll Number and the password generated at the time of registration.
New candidates must pay the non-refundable counselling fee (Rs. 400 or Rs. 250, as applicable) via Net Banking, Debit/Credit Card, or UPI.
Download and check the institute-wise vacant seat matrix released on September 21, 2026, to see the number of seats available in each category.
Add your preferred nursing institutes from the list shown, arranging them in your personal order of priority (the college you want most should be your 1st preference).
Review the choice order carefully.
Click "Save" and lock your preferences before the deadline of September 23, 2026.

sections.heading: Important Instructions for Candidates

items: Prioritize college preferences carefully before submitting, as choices determine seat allotment.
Choice filling and registration close on September 23, 2026 - there is no indication in the source of an extension.
Unlocked choices are auto-locked by the system using the last saved version, so save your preferences before the deadline even if you plan to make further edits.
Keep the counselling fee payment receipt and login credentials safe for future reference.
Report to the allotted college within the specified verification window (September 26-30, 2026) to avoid losing the allotted seat.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: Choose an option when the allotment comes out. In Round 1, KEA warned that candidates who don’t select a choice within the deadline are treated as not interested in the seat and moved to choice-4. Don’t miss the window.

Choice-1 means fee, slip and reporting. Choice-1 candidates must download the seat confirmation slip and report to the allotted college by the stated deadline. Pay the fee online before that, because the allotment is cancelled if you skip any of these steps.

Surrendering a seat may need an in-person visit. For Round 1, KEA required that candidates surrendering a choice 1 or 2 seat do so in person at the KEA office in Bengaluru by a fixed time. Check whether Round 4 uses the same rule.

Later rounds may have fewer choices. In Round 1 candidates had all four choice options available. In later UGCET rounds, KEA said choices 2 and 3 would not be available. NEET Round 4 may be similarly restricted, so read the choice rules in the notice carefully.

Keep your documents and the official schedule at hand. Carry your NEET UG 2026 scorecard and admit card, along with the allotment letter and fee receipt. KEA often extends deadlines, but don’t count on it. Follow only kea.kar.nic.in for dates.

How to Apply for CEE Kerala DNB Post MBBS 2026?

content.text: CEE Kerala has specified five mandatory application steps.

items: Visit the official DNB Post MBBS 2026 application portal.
Click Registration and enter the required mobile number and email address.
Create a password and save the system-generated application number.
Log in using the application number and password.
Complete the application form with personal, educational, NEET PG and applicable Government service details.
Pay the prescribed application fee of Rs. 1,000 plus gateway charges.
Upload the required images and certificates.
Complete option registration by selecting the applicable course, speciality and institution preferences.
Review the completed application and option details.
Download or print the acknowledgement page for future reference.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: Eligibility is limited. All the State quota seats are earmarked for In-Service candidates (Medical Education, Health Service or Insurance Medical Service of the Govt. of Kerala), and you must hold an MBBS degree.

Apply online only, on the CEE website. The 2025 round let candidates apply online through the CEE website until 06.11.2025, 12.00 PM. The 2026 deadline will be in the new notification, and no late submissions are accepted.
The fee is Rs 1,000, paid online. In earlier rounds, it was non-refundable. The 2026 Post Diploma notice says payment is by credit card, debit card or net banking.

Upload your documents with the application. After paying, you must upload your photo, signature and the required certificates, such as proof of nativity. Nothing can be submitted after the last date, so have all of it scanned in advance.

Register your options and skip the printout. You must select and order your options (speciality and institution combinations) as part of the online application, and the application is complete only after options are registered. There is no need to send a printout of the acknowledgement page or any documents to the CEE office. Still, save the acknowledgement page for your records.

sections.heading: How to Complete Kerala PG Dental Admission 2026 Option Entry?

content.text: The earlier Round 3 option registration window ended on 12 October 2026. The following steps explain the procedure prescribed in the official notification for that window.

items: Visit the official website at cee.kerala.gov.in.
Open the PG Dental 2026 Candidate Portal.
Enter the application number and password to log in.
Select the Option Registration menu.
Choose the preferred MDS courses and dental colleges.
Arrange the options according to admission preference.
Pay the applicable option registration fee.
Complete the option registration process within the prescribed deadline.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: Check the deadline first. Log in to the “PG Dental 2026 - Candidate Portal” with your application number and password, then open “Option Registration”. Confirm the current closing date and time on the CEE notification, because deadlines are often extended.

Fresh options need a fresh fee. Fresh option registration is available in the third (final) round, but with a fresh option registration fee. Earlier-round fees are forfeited if you were allotted a seat in Round 2 and did not report, did not join, or quit after joining.

Fill options in strict order of preference. Choose course and college combinations carefully. Allotment follows your rank, category and the order of your list, so put your most-wanted choices first and don’t add colleges you wouldn’t join.
Save and confirm your list. Unconfirmed or unsaved options may not be considered. Take a printout or screenshot of the final list.

Prepare to join if allotted. Download the allotment memo, pay the fee or balance fee, and report to the college within the joining dates. Keep your original documents ready, including your Kerala State Dental Council registration, as admission requires the original.

detail.title: Nagaland University FYUGP Admission 2026 - Key Highlights
detail.short_info: Nagaland University UG Admission 2026 is open for FYUGP B.Sc. Honours courses via CUET-UG. Check eligibility, important dates, application process, documents, and how to apply online before 15th July 2026.

content.text: Nagaland University, the only Central University in Nagaland, has opened undergraduate admissions for the 2026-27 academic session under its Four-Year Undergraduate Programme (FYUGP) in B.Sc. Honours and B.Sc. Honours with Research. Admission is based on CUET-UG 2026 scores combined with Class XII marks, and eligible candidates can apply online at admission.nagalanduniversity.ac.in until 15th July 2026.

This guide covers everything applicants need to know eligibility, courses on offer, the full admission timeline, required documents, reservation categories, and how to apply, based entirely on the university's official admission notice.

links.text: Nagaland University FYUGP Admission 2026

sections.heading: Nagaland University FYUGP Admission 2026 - Key Highlights

content.text: Here's a quick snapshot of the admission cycle for candidates who want the essential facts at a glance before reading the detailed sections below.

sections.heading: Courses Offered Under FYUGP 2026

content.text: Applicants often want to know exactly which subjects and programme formats are available before applying. Here is what Nagaland University is offering this year.

The admissions are conducted by the University's Multi-Disciplinary Research Centre (MDRC) in accordance with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 framework. Under this framework, the undergraduate programme offers students the flexibility to pursue Honours and Honours with Research programmes in five science disciplines Botany, Chemistry, Mathematics, Physics, and Zoology.

sections.heading: Disciplines available under FYUGP B.Sc.:

items: Botany
Chemistry
Mathematics
Physics
Zoology

content.text: Students can choose either the standard Honours track or the research-intensive Honours with Research track in any of these five subjects, in line with the NEP 2020 multidisciplinary model.

sections.heading: Eligibility Criteria for Nagaland University UG Admission 2026

content.text: Before applying, candidates should understand how selection works, since Nagaland University does not rely on Class XII marks alone.

Admissions will be granted strictly on merit based on candidates' CUET-UG scores and Class XII examination performance, as per the eligibility criteria prescribed by the respective academic departments. This means:

items: Candidates must have appeared for CUET-UG 2026 in the relevant subject combination.
Final merit is a combination of the CUET-UG score and Class XII marks.
Department-specific eligibility norms (such as required subjects in Class XII) apply, so applicants should check the specific requirements for their chosen discipline on the official portal.

sections.heading: Nagaland University UG Admission 2026: Important Dates

content.text: Timing matters a great deal in this admission cycle, as the entire process from application to final seat allotment runs on a tight schedule. The section below lays out every key date candidates need to track.

Applications are open till 15th July 2026 for FYUGP B.Sc. Honours and Honours with Research programmes. The University will publish the list of shortlisted candidates on 16th July 2026, while admissions for selected candidates will be conducted from 17th July to 20th July 2026. Admissions from the waiting list are scheduled from 21st July to 23rd July 2026.
Candidates are advised to keep checking the official admission portal regularly, as revised or extended dates (if any) are typically notified there first.

sections.heading: How to Apply for Nagaland University FYUGP Admission 2026

content.text: Applicants naturally want a simple, step-by-step way to submit their application without missing any part of the process. Here's how it works.
Interested candidates can submit their applications through the University's admission portal at admission.nagalanduniversity.ac.in. The general process is as follows:

items: Visit the official admission portal: admission.nagalanduniversity.ac.in
Register with basic personal details to create a login.
Log in and select the FYUGP B.Sc. Honours/Honours with Research programme.
Choose your preferred discipline (Botany, Chemistry, Mathematics, Physics, or Zoology).
Fill in academic details, including Class X and Class XII information and CUET-UG scorecard details.
Upload the required documents (see checklist below).
Review the form carefully before final submission, as incomplete or incorrect forms may be rejected.
Submit the application within the deadline of 15th July 2026.

sections.heading: Documents Required for Application

content.text: Missing or incorrect documents are one of the most common reasons applications get delayed or rejected, so it's worth checking this list closely before starting the form.

Applicants are required to submit a recent passport-size photograph and signature, Class X admit card and marksheet, Class XII admit card and marksheet, CUET scorecard, transfer certificate, and other applicable documents such as caste, disability, backward tribe, or gap certificates, wherever relevant.

sections.heading: Document checklist:

items: Recent passport-size photograph
Signature (scanned copy)
Class X admit card and marksheet
Class XII admit card and marksheet
CUET-UG scorecard
Transfer certificate
Caste certificate (if applicable)
Disability certificate (if applicable)
Backward tribe certificate (if applicable)
Gap certificate (if applicable)

sections.heading: Reservation Categories and Seat Allocation

content.text: Reservation norms directly affect how seats are distributed, so candidates belonging to specific categories should know exactly where they stand in the process.

Seat allocation will be carried out in accordance with the norms and reservation guidelines of Nagaland University under categories including Scheduled Tribe (ST), Scheduled Caste (SC), Other Backward Classes (OBC), Persons with Disabilities (PwD), Economically Weaker Sections (EWS), Sports Quota, Employees' Quota, and Unreserved (UR).

sections.heading: Campus Facilities for FYUGP Students

content.text: Beyond academics, prospective students and parents often want to know what kind of campus life and support infrastructure to expect at Nagaland University.

Students admitted to the programme will have access to well-equipped laboratories, digital library resources, Wi-Fi-enabled campus facilities, e-learning support, sports infrastructure, career counselling and placement assistance, as well as on-campus cafeteria and health centre facilities.

sections.heading: Key facilities include:

items: Well-equipped science laboratories
Digital library resources
Wi-Fi-enabled campus
E-learning support
Sports infrastructure
Career counselling and placement assistance
On-campus cafeteria
Health centre

sections.heading: What the Vice Chancellor Says About FYUGP 2026

content.text: University leadership statements often clarify the intent and vision behind a new admission cycle, which can help applicants understand what the programme is designed to deliver.

Welcoming applicants to the programme, Prof. Jagadish K Patnaik, Vice Chancellor of Nagaland University, invited students from across India to join the university, noting its status as the only Central University in the State of Nagaland and highlighting the implementation of FYUGP under NEP 2020 to provide a multidisciplinary, research-oriented, and student-centric learning environment. He further described admission through CUET-UG 2026 as ensuring a transparent, fair, and merit-based process that enables talented students from across the country to join the university's academic community, with B.Sc. Honours and Honours with Research programmes combining rigorous academic training with hands-on research, innovation, and skill development.

sections.heading: Contact Details for Admission Queries

content.text: Candidates who run into issues while filling the form or have questions about eligibility should reach out directly to the department handling this admission cycle.
For admission-related queries, applicants may contact the Multi-Disciplinary Research Centre at +91 9170707089 or write to [email protected].

content.text: Follow these steps to check and download your Odisha CT Entrance scorecard:

items: Visit the official SAMS Odisha website: scert.samsodisha.gov.in.
Look for the notice reading "CT Result & Score Card are now live" on the homepage, or find the "D.El.Ed" section and click on the Score Card link.

sections.heading: What Happens After the Odisha D.El.Ed Result: Counselling Process

content.text: Once the merit list and cut-off marks are released, SCERT Odisha is expected to conduct counselling and seat allotment for admission into the two-year D.El.Ed programme. Based on how this process is generally run for SAMS Odisha admissions, it typically includes:

items: Counselling Registration: Eligible candidates register for counselling on scert.samsodisha.gov.in during the notified window.
Choice Filling: Candidates fill and lock their preferred DIETs, BIETs, or ETEIs (teacher training institutes) in order of preference.
Seat Allotment: Seats are allotted based on rank, category, and choices filled.
Document Verification: Candidates report to the allotted institute with original documents for verification.
Admission Fee Payment: Candidates confirm their seat by paying the applicable admission fee within the given deadline.

sections.heading: Important Instructions for Candidates

items: Cross-check all details on the scorecard, including name, roll number, and marks obtained. Report any discrepancy to SCERT Odisha promptly.
Save and print your scorecard immediately while the link is live, since result links on such portals are sometimes moved once the checking window closes.
Rely only on the official website, scert.samsodisha.gov.in, or official SAMS Odisha communication for result and counselling updates.

detail.short_info: Odisha NEET Merit List 2026 is out at ojee.nic.in. Check the provisional merit list released date 13 August 2026, how to raise a grievance by 3 PM on 14 Aug, final merit list timing, choice-filling dates, eligibility, fees, and step-by-step download process for MBBS/BDS state quota counselling 2026-27.

content.text: Odisha NEET Merit List 2026 has been released by the Odisha Joint Entrance Examination (OJEE) Cell. The provisional state merit list for MBBS/BDS admission under the 85% state quota was published on 13 August 2026, and candidates who have concerns about their rank, category, or eligibility can raise a grievance before the final list is published on 14 August 2026. This article explains the release date, how to download the merit list, the grievance/objection process, choice-filling schedule, eligibility, fees, and answers to common questions candidates are searching for.

sections.heading: How to Submit Grievances on Odisha NEET Merit List 2026 (Till August 14)

content.text: If a candidate finds any discrepancy in the provisional merit list - such as an incorrect NEET rank, wrong category, missing name, or a data-entry error - OJEE has provided a formal grievance-redressal window before the final list is locked. As per the official notice, the process is as follows:

items: Prepare a written representation clearly describing the discrepancy in the provisional merit list.
Attach relevant supporting documentary evidence (such as scorecards, category certificates, or admit cards) along with the representation.
Email the representation to [email protected].
Ensure the email is sent on or before 14 August 2026, 3:00 PM. Representations received after this date and time will not be considered.
Continue checking ojee.nic.in and odishajee.com for confirmation and further notices.

content.text: Candidates should note that the general counselling schedule notice had earlier indicated a query window ending at 11:30 AM on 14 August 2026, while the dedicated grievance notice issued on 13 August 2026 specifies the deadline as 3:00 PM the same day. Since the dedicated notice was issued specifically for this purpose, candidates are advised to treat 3:00 PM on 14 August 2026 as the operative deadline, while still submitting objections as early as possible.

sections.heading: Reservation Structure for 2026-27 (State Quota)

content.text: Multiple sources reporting on the 2026-27 admission cycle indicate that Odisha has revised its state-quota reservation matrix, with an increase in ST and SC reservation and the introduction of a new SEBC category. Candidates should verify the exact percentages against the official OJEE counselling brochure, as this article could not independently confirm the figures from a primary OJEE notice at the time of writing.

sections.heading: How to Download the Odisha NEET Merit List 2026

items: Visit the official website ojee.nic.in or odishajee.com.
Go to the MBBS/BDS Counselling section on the homepage.
Click on the notice titled "Provisional State Merit List for MBBS/BDS Admission 2026-27" (or the "Final State Merit List" link once published).
The merit list will open as a PDF document.
Use Ctrl+F (or Cmd+F on Mac) to search your NEET application number, roll number, or name.
Check your All India Rank, state rank, category, and eligibility status.
Download and save the PDF, or take a printout for future reference during choice filling and reporting.

sections.heading: Important Instructions for Candidates

items: Being listed on the merit list does not guarantee a seat; final allotment depends on document verification, category, rank, and seat availability.
Grievances on the provisional merit list must reach OJEE by email before the stated deadline; late submissions will not be entertained.

PWD/PC and Ex-Servicemen candidates must attend their respective assessment boards on the notified dates to claim reservation benefits; missing these dates results in loss of that reservation category.
Choices, once locked in a round, cannot be altered under any circumstances.
Candidates should regularly check ojee.nic.in and odishajee.com, as OJEE frequently issues updated or corrigendum notices.

sections.heading: IISER IAT 2026 Important Dates
How Is the Round 3 Seat Allotment Decided?

content.text: Seat allotment in every round, including Round 3, is based on:

items: The candidate's IAT 2026 All India Rank (AIR) and category rank
The order of institute/programme preferences submitted during choice filling
Seat availability at the time of that round, including seats vacated by candidates who did not accept earlier offers

sections.heading: How to Check the IISER IAT Round 3 Seat Allotment Result 2026

items: Visit the official website, iiseradmission.in.
Locate and click the link for the IISER IAT 2026 Round 3 seat allotment result.

Submit the details to view your Round 3 allotment status.

sections.heading: After the Result: Accept, Float, or Freeze

content.text: Candidates who receive a seat in Round 3 typically have the following options, consistent with how earlier rounds of the 2026 cycle have been run:

rows: Accept the current seat and exit further allotment rounds; no further upgradation.
Retain the currently allotted seat while remaining eligible for a higher-preference institute/programme in later rounds.
Stay within the same institute but remain open to a better programme, if available in a later round.

content.text: Whichever option is chosen, candidates allotted a seat must pay the Seat Acceptance Fee (SAF) within the round's deadline to hold the seat. In the previous (2025) cycle, the SAF was reported as Rs 35,000 for general category candidates and Rs 17,500 for SC/ST candidates; the exact 2026 SAF amount for Round 3 was not confirmed in the sources reviewed, so candidates should verify the current figure on the official portal before making payment.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: The result is accessible only through candidate login on iiseradmission.in - there is no public result page where you can check status using just a roll number.
Missing the August 13, 2026 acceptance/reporting deadline for Round 3 can lead to cancellation of the allotted seat.
The counselling process is entirely online except for the final physical reporting stage at the allotted institute.
Do not rely solely on third-party websites for dates and fee amounts - always cross-check with the official portal.

sections.heading: What Is IISER Counselling 2026?

content.text: IISER Counselling 2026 is the centralised online admission process conducted by the Joint Admissions Committee (JAC), with IISER Berhampur serving as the organising institute for this admission cycle. The process facilitates admission to BS-MS, BS, and B.Tech programmes offered by the seven participating IISER campuses, based on candidates' IAT 2026 ranks, categories, and the choices filled during registration. sections.heading: Seat Acceptance Fee (SAF) 2026

content.text: Candidates who receive a seat allotment must pay the Seat Acceptance Fee within the round-wise deadline to confirm their admission. The SAF amount is category-based:

rows: General, EWS, OBC-NCL, PwD, Kashmiri Migrants (KM), Kashmiri Pandit/Kashmiri Hindu Families (Non-Migrants)

content.text: The remaining amount (after deducting the non-refundable administrative fee) is adjusted against the first-semester tuition fee at the IISER the candidate joins. If the SAF is not paid within the deadline, the allotted seat will be cancelled and the candidate will not be considered in subsequent rounds.

sections.heading: Freeze and Float Options Explained

content.text: After accepting a seat, candidates must choose between two options:

items: Freeze: Accept the current seat permanently and exit further rounds of counselling. No further upgradation will be considered.
Float: Retain the current allotted seat while remaining eligible for an upgrade to a more preferred campus or programme in later rounds, if a vacancy arises.

content.text: Candidates who do not respond within the deadline, or who choose to decline the offer, may still be considered in subsequent rounds subject to merit and seat availability, as per available reports - though candidates should verify this rule for their specific case on the official portal, since the exact treatment of "no response" cases in the 2026 cycle is not explicitly detailed in the source notification.

As of 4 August 2026, the portal showed more than 3,400 completed applications.

sections.heading: Puducherry UG Medical Counselling 2026: Application Fee

rows: NRI / NRI-Sponsored / OCI / OCI-Sponsored / Foreign National

content.text: Payment is accepted online only. A single candidate may submit only one application; submitting more than one leads to cancellation of both.

sections.heading: Documents and Certificate Dating Rules

content.text: Candidates claiming Puducherry residency must upload renewed certificates issued on or after 1 January 2026, including:

items: Residence certificate
Community certificate (Note: community certificates issued in the Central Educational Institutions format are not accepted)

content.text: For EWS and income certificates, the certificate must be issued on or after 1 April 2026.
Where applicable, candidates must also upload:

items: Regional reservation certificates (for Karaikal, Mahe, and Yanam candidates)
Special reservation certificates: freedom fighter, PwBD, ex-servicemen, Meritorious Sports Person (MSP), and government school categories

sections.heading: Guidelines for MSP and PwBD Candidates

content.text: CENTAC published separate guidelines on 31 July 2026 for the Meritorious Sports Persons (MSP) quota and for assessment of Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) under the Government Quota.

items: MSP applicants from the Puducherry region must hand-deliver self-attested copies of sports certificates, along with a copy of the application, at the CENTAC office, Kamarajar Manimandapam, by 6 August 2026, 5:00 PM.
MSP candidates from Karaikal, Mahe, and Yanam must upload a single self-attested PDF through their login dashboard by the same deadline.

sections.heading: Cross-State AYUSH Option for Puducherry Candidates

content.text: CENTAC has also invited applications from Puducherry candidates for BSMS, BUMS, and BHMS courses in government Indian Medicine and Homoeopathy colleges in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka. The original notification was issued on 21 July 2026, and the last date was extended through a notice dated 31 July 2026. Candidates should check the revised deadline directly on the portal before applying, as the exact extended date was not specified in the source reviewed for this article (Not Available Officially).

sections.heading: Puducherry NEET UG 2026: Topper Details

content.text: Krishanth Abhinav M topped the Union Territory of Puducherry in the Re-NEET UG 2026 result, securing All India Rank (AIR) 553 with a percentile of 99.9721, as reported by exam-tracking sources including Aakash Institute and Daily Jagran.

Source conflict note: Moneycontrol has separately reported that the Puducherry topper scored 670 marks. This specific marks figure could not be independently cross-verified against a second source at the time of writing, so it is presented here as reported by Moneycontrol rather than as a confirmed official figure. Candidates should treat the AIR/percentile (cross-verified across two sources) as more reliable than the marks figure until the official NTA scorecard or CENTAC records are checked directly.

sections.heading: Important Instructions for Applicants

items: Only one application per candidate is permitted; multiple applications result in cancellation.
Applications and objections must be submitted only through the official portals or email listed in this article.
Keep renewed residence, community, EWS/income, and category certificates ready with the correct issue dates before starting the application.
False nativity or residency claims across multiple states can lead to rejection and legal action.
Since the seat matrix and full counselling schedule are still awaited, candidates should check centacpuducherry.in regularly for updates rather than relying on unofficial estimates.
