how_to_apply: Candidates can apply only through the offline postal route. Each applicant can submit only one application indicating a specific Trade and Station.
Type the application form neatly on A4 size paper using Arial font, size 12, as per Appendix 'A', and print it double-sided.
Fill in the required personal, educational, technical, and trade details in block letters, signing every page of the application.
Affix one recent coloured self-attested passport size photograph in the application form and self-signed photographs on each of the two Admit Cards (Appendix 'B').

Attach self-attested copies of all required certificates (Aadhaar, birth certificate, qualification, ITI certificates, experience, caste/EWS/ESM if applicable) along with signed examination instructions (Appendix 'C').
Enclose one self-addressed envelope of size 30 cms x 12 cms affixed with a postal stamp of Rs 60/- for dispatch of the admit card.
Superscribe the main envelope clearly as "APPLICATION FOR THE POST OF TECHNICIAN (SKILLED)" or "APPLICATION FOR THE POST OF TECHNICIAN (SEMI SKILLED)".

Send the application packet by ordinary post or Speed Post to: The Controller, Controllerate of Quality Assurance (General Stores), DGQA Stores Complex, Ashok Path, Meerpur Cantt, Kanpur – 208004, Uttar Pradesh.
important_instructions: Submitting more than one application will lead to summary rejection of all applications without assigning any cause. Selected candidates will be appointed on probation for a period of two years and are liable to serve anywhere within India. No change in post or posting station will be permitted after submission of the application. Candidates diagnosed with night blindness or colour blindness will be declared medically unfit and cannot be appointed. Ex-Servicemen and Agniveers who have already secured regular civil employment in Group 'C' or 'D' posts under Central or State Government under ESM reservation quota are not eligible for reservation under ESM/Agniveer quota. Government servants must forward applications through proper channel along with NOC; otherwise, applications will be summarily rejected. No TA or DA will be paid for appearing in the Written Test or Trade Test. Candidates must make their own arrangements for lodging and boarding. The candidate must disclose any higher qualification possessed; failure to do so will lead to disqualification. The photo in the Application Form and Admit Card must be identical and should not have been taken earlier than one month prior to submitting the application. Overwriting, striking out, or using correction fluid on the application form is strictly prohibited; candidates are advised to type the application form.

Affix one recent coloured self-attested passport size photograph in the application form and self-signed photographs on each of the two Admit Cards (Appendix 'B'). Attach self-attested copies of all required certificates (Aadhaar, birth certificate, qualification, ITI certificates, experience, caste/EWS/ESM if applicable) along with signed examination instructions (Appendix 'C'). Enclose one self-addressed envelope of size 30 cms x 12 cms affixed with a postal stamp of Rs 60/- for dispatch of the admit card. Superscribe the main envelope clearly as "APPLICATION FOR THE POST OF TECHNICIAN (SKILLED)" or "APPLICATION FOR THE POST OF TECHNICIAN (SEMI SKILLED)". Send the application packet by ordinary post or Speed Post to: The Controller, Controllerate of Quality Assurance (General Stores), DGQA Stores Complex, Ashok Path, Meerpur Cantt, Kanpur – 208004, Uttar Pradesh.

content_sections.heading: Documents Required
content_sections.text: The following documents must be enclosed along with the application form: Duly completed Application Form (Appendix 'A') typed in English on A4 paper Two Admit Cards (Appendix 'B') on A4 size paper One self-addressed envelope (30 cm x 12 cm) affixed with Rs. 60/- postal stamp Three recent passport size photographs (one on application form, two self-signed on admit cards) NOC from Head of Office/Establishment for candidates serving in Government/PSU Self-attested copy of Aadhaar Card Self-attested copy of Birth Certificate Self-attested copies of Technical Qualification (ITI Pass Certificate) Self-attested copies of Educational Qualification (Matriculation and higher) Experience Certificate (if applicable) Self-attested copy of Caste Certificate (OBC/SC/ST) / EWS Certificate / Discharge Certificate or e-PPO for ESM or Agniveer Instructions for Examination duly signed by the applicant (Appendix 'C')

content_sections.heading: DGQA Important Instructions
content_sections.text: Submitting more than one application will lead to summary rejection of all applications without assigning any cause. Selected candidates will be appointed on probation for a period of two years and are liable to serve anywhere within India. No change in post or posting station will be permitted after submission of the application. Candidates diagnosed with night blindness or colour blindness will be declared medically unfit and cannot be appointed. Ex-Servicemen and Agniveers who have already secured regular civil employment in Group 'C' or 'D' posts under Central or State Government under ESM reservation quota are not eligible for reservation under ESM/Agniveer quota. Government servants must forward applications through proper channel along with NOC; otherwise, applications will be summarily rejected. No TA or DA will be paid for appearing in the Written Test or Trade Test. Candidates must make their own arrangements for lodging and boarding. The candidate must disclose any higher qualification possessed; failure to do so will lead to disqualification. The photo in the Application Form and Admit Card must be identical and should not have been taken earlier than one month prior to submitting the application. Overwriting, striking out, or using correction fluid on the application form is strictly prohibited; candidates are advised to type the application form.

content_sections.heading: DLSA Jalore Para Legal Volunteer Job Description
content_sections.text: Selected Para Legal Volunteers ( अधिकार मित्र ) will perform the following duties in their villages, wards, and neighborhoods: Educate citizens on living a dignified life and make them aware of their constitutional and legal rights and duties. Assist citizens in resolving disputes and problems by connecting them with legal services authorities or mediation centres. Assist the DLSA or Taluka Legal Services Committee in organizing legal awareness camps. Provide information on ongoing state and central legal aid schemes, the National Legal Services Authority, and the High Court Legal Services Committee, and ensure free legal services reach eligible persons. Encourage pre-litigation settlement of disputes through DLSA or Taluka Legal Services Committees without any court fee or expenses, explaining that lok adalats can settle matters amicably without cost. Guide citizens on utility services (transport, post, electricity, water, sanitation, banking, housing, and land records) for settlement through permanent lok adalats without court fees. Disseminate information regarding welfare schemes implemented by the central and state governments at prominent public places. Actively support legal aid clinics established in their area. Make vulnerable sections of society aware of their rights and assist victims of crime with compensation under Section 357-A / 396 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. Visit jails, lock-ups, observation homes, and de-addiction hospitals upon authorization to apprise inmates of their legal rights. Provide information regarding pre-litigation counseling, alternate dispute resolution, and lok adalats. Submit a monthly report or report of activities to the chairperson of the DLSA or Taluka Legal Services Committee by the 2nd of the following month.

content_sections.heading: Enclosures
content_sections.text: Candidates must attach self-attested copies of the following documents with their application: Verified copy of Secondary (10th) marksheet or certificate for proof of date of birth. Verified copy of educational qualification certificates. Latest original character certificate not older than 6 months issued by a respectable person. Self-attested passport-size photograph pasted on the application form (do not staple). Verified copy of Bonafide Resident Certificate. Document supporting local residency in the village or ward where application is made (Aadhaar Card, Ration Card, Voter ID Card, Bonafide Resident Certificate, or equivalent proof). Self-declaration affidavit stating that no criminal case is pending against the applicant.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: Applications received will be scrutinized. Eligible candidates will be called for an interview. Successful candidates in the interview will undergo training as Para Legal Volunteers.

how_to_apply: Visit the official JKSSB website at www.jkssb.nic.in once the application window opens on 05.10.2026.
Register/login on the online application portal as instructed on the website.
Fill in personal, educational, and category details carefully in the online application form.
Upload live photograph and signature as per the prescribed size (10 KB to 20 KB).
Pay the application fee online through Net Banking, Credit Card, or Debit Card.
Review all entries carefully before final submission, as no corrections are allowed after submission.
Submit the form and save/print the application for future reference and Document Verification.
JKSSB Class-IV Apply Online link will be activated on the official website from 14.10.2026 to 12.11.2026.
important_instructions: Only one online application per item number is allowed; a candidate submitting multiple applications for the same item number will have their candidature cancelled. Candidates must carry valid original photo ID proof and two recent passport photographs to the examination hall. Mobile phones, smart watches, smart glasses, AI-enabled devices, and other electronic/communication devices are strictly prohibited in the examination hall. content_sections.heading: JKSSB Class-IV Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: Candidates applying for JKSSB Class-IV (MTS) & Sanitation Worker Recruitment 2026 must satisfy the domicile, qualification, and age conditions below, all assessed as on the cut-off date of 03.11.2026 (or 01.01.2026 for age). content_sections.heading: JKSSB Class-IV Age Limit
content_sections.text: The age of candidates is reckoned as on 01.01.2026. Ex-Servicemen may deduct their period of Armed Forces service from actual age; if the resultant age doesn't exceed the post's maximum limit by more than 3 years, they are deemed to satisfy the age condition. An additional 5-year relaxation in upper age limit is available to candidates claiming the casual-worker additional weightage benefit under the J&K Appointment to Class IV (Special Recruitment) Rules, 2020. content_sections.heading: JKSSB Class-IV Salary

content_sections.heading: JKSSB Class-IV Selection Process
content_sections.text: Selection for JKSSB Class-IV (MTS) & Sanitation Worker Recruitment 2026 will be based on an Objective Type Written Test followed by Document Verification, with the overall merit determined using written test marks plus additional weightage points. Written examination will consist of Objective Type, Multiple Choice Questions set in English only. Negative marking applies: one-fourth of the marks assigned to a question is deducted for each wrong answer. Total marks are distributed between the written test and additional weightage points, and the split differs by cadre as shown below. Cadre and Department allocation for successful candidates will be done on a merit-cum-preference basis, and once notified, allocation decisions are final and binding. Original and self-attested photocopies of the online application form and all certificates. Domicile Certificate (valid as on the cut-off date). Educational qualification certificates. Category/Reservation certificate in the prescribed format, if applicable. Two recent passport-size colour photographs (not older than 6 months) and a valid photo ID proof. Certificates supporting any weightage claim (no-government-family-member, widow/divorced/orphan status, or casual-worker status), where applicable.

how_to_apply: The notification allows only the online application system. Applications sent by any other means are not accepted. Candidates should read the full advertisement before applying.

Visit the Commission's website upsssc.gov.in and, on the homepage under the Live Advertisement Segment, click the advertisement for Sports Directorate Main Examination (PET-2025)/22 to view or download it.
Log in using your PET-2025 registration number. An OTP is sent to the mobile number or e-mail registered in PET-2025.

Your personal details recorded in PET-2025 (name, parents' names, domicile, category, EWS, horizontal reservation details, date of birth, gender, marital status, mobile number, e-mail) are displayed automatically.
Select the posts you want to apply for. A post not selected is not considered.

For each selected post, choose Yes or No for the required educational qualification and enter the board or university name, year of passing, certificate or roll number, certificate issue date and marks details.

Check the photo and signature uploaded in PET-2025, which are displayed automatically and cannot be changed. Then enter whether you hold any preferential qualification, and check your permanent and correspondence address.
Read the declaration, tick all checkboxes, enter the verification code and click "Save and Submit".
Pay the fee through credit card, debit card, internet banking, UPI or SBI e-challan. The application is submitted automatically once the fee is paid and reconciled.
Download and print the application. Keep a copy safe, as it may be required during record verification.

If the application does not appear after payment, the fee has not been reconciled. Log in with the registration number, use "Update Your Transaction ID by Double Verification" in the Applicant Segment, and click "Verify Transaction ID".
If payment fails, a Payment Acknowledgment Receipt (PAR) appears instead of the application. Use the same option and then the "Application Fee Deposition" option to pay.
For SBI e-challan, download the challan, pay at any SBI branch, then enter the challan details through the "Update Your Transaction ID by Double Verification" option.

After the application is finally submitted, candidates can make corrections until 11-11-2026 by logging in through the Applicant's Dashboard, clicking "Modify Application" and entering the verification code and OTP. Only the following details can be corrected:
Correspondence address.
Personal details such as EWS and horizontal reservation category (Dependant of Freedom Fighter, Disabled, Ex-Servicemen, Gender, Outstanding Sportsperson, etc.).
Details of mandatory or preferential qualification entered in the application.
Marital status.
No correction is possible after the last date for correction, and the Commission does not accept separate representations for corrections.
important_instructions: Uttar Pradesh reserved-category candidates must mark their category in the application. Candidates working in central or state government service must get a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from their employer, to be shown when the Commission asks. Self-attested copies of mark sheets, certificates and degrees must be produced to verify age and qualification when requested. The examination date, time and centre are given in the admission card. The centre, date and time are not changed in any case, and candidates should not write to the Commission about it. The Commission does not correspond individually with candidates. All information is uploaded on its website, so candidates should check it regularly. An application can be cancelled if the date of birth is not given, the candidate is overage or underage, lacks the mandatory qualification, or gives false information. Giving wrong facts that cannot be proved by certificates can lead to debarment from this and all other examinations and selections of the Commission. Malpractice, indiscipline or misbehaviour in the examination can lead to cancellation of candidature and debarment. The Uttar Pradesh Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 applies.

content_sections.text: Only those candidates can apply online who hold the mandatory qualification for the advertised post, appeared in the Preliminary Eligibility Test (PET) 2025, and have a PET-2025 scorecard issued by the Commission. The notification also lists these general conditions: Applicants must be citizens of India. Candidates must hold the mandatory educational qualification and other required eligibility, with the relevant certificates, by the last date of application, 04-11-2026. Candidates for the Main Examination are shortlisted on the normalized score of PET-2025. Candidates with zero, negative or less-than-zero absolute or normalized score are not shortlisted. Candidates whose PET-2025 results are marked "Under Investigation (UI)" or "Provisional" are allowed to apply provisionally. Their shortlisting and selection depend on the outcome of the Commission's inquiry. Only one application is to be submitted for the advertised posts. If more than one is submitted, the last submitted application is accepted and the others are treated as cancelled. Candidates must check that they meet the eligibility conditions before applying. The Commission does not advise candidates on their eligibility. Male candidates with more than one living wife, and female candidates married to a man who already has a living wife, are not considered eligible unless the Governor has granted an exemption.

content_sections.heading: Reservation Provisions in UPSSSC Sports Directorate Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Reservation applies to Uttar Pradesh SC, ST, OBC and EWS candidates as per the latest Uttar Pradesh government orders and the requisition received from the department. EWS candidates must have family income from all sources below Rs. 8 lakh in the financial year before the year of application and must meet the conditions of the Uttar Pradesh Public Services (Reservation for Economically Weaker Sections) Act, 2020 (10 percent reservation). They need an EWS certificate issued between 01-04-2026 and 04-11-2026, based on FY 2025-26 income and valid for FY 2026-27, in the prescribed format. Candidates who are not original residents of Uttar Pradesh do not get reservation and are treated as Unreserved. A candidate claiming more than one reservation gets only one benefit, whichever is more beneficial. Ex-Servicemen must have retired from service by 04-11-2026. Dependants of Freedom Fighters and Ex-Servicemen get reservation under the Uttar Pradesh Public Services (Physically Handicapped, Dependants of Freedom Fighters and Ex-Servicemen) Reservation Act, 1993, as amended. Women of Uttar Pradesh are placed in the categories to which they belong. For Uttar Pradesh women candidates, only a caste certificate issued on the father's side is valid. Women's reservation is subject to the final decision of the Supreme Court in Special Appeal (D) No. 475/2019. Uttar Pradesh Outstanding Sportspersons must submit a certificate in the format prescribed by the competent authority, under the Uttar Pradesh Government Departments (Direct Recruitment to Group-C Posts of Outstanding Sportspersons) Rules, 2022. Persons with disabilities must hold a disability certificate issued by the competent authority in the prescribed format, stating the type and percentage of disability. The notification says posts have been re-identified to ensure 4 percent horizontal reservation, and disabled candidates must update their disability category and sub-category in the application. Candidates selected under horizontal reservation are adjusted in their own category. The notification attaches formats for the SC/ST caste certificate, OBC caste certificate, EWS income and asset certificate and self-declaration, dependant of freedom fighter certificate, and disability certificate forms (Appendix 1 to 9 and Annexure 1 to 2).

content_sections.text: The selection process consists of three stages: Stage-I Screening test (written examination), Stage-II Driving test, and Stage-III Interview/Viva-Voce. Candidates equal to 5 times the number of vacancies (1:5) in order of merit in the screening test will be called for the driving test. Candidates must secure at least 50% marks (20 out of 40) to qualify. Candidates equal to 3 times the number of vacancies (1:3) in order of merit in the driving test will be called for the interview. Stage-III Interview/Viva-Voce (20 marks): Includes viva-voce and document verification. Candidates must secure at least 60% marks (12 out of 20) to qualify. Final selection is based on the total marks obtained in the driving test and interview.

Date of birth

Candidates will be allowed to take the examination at the centre specified in the Admit Card only and at no other centre. They are advised to report at the examination centre one hour before the commencement of the examination.
No candidate will be admitted to the examination unless he/she holds a valid Admit Card, and no candidate will be admitted to the examination hall after the commencement of the examination.
The candidate should not bring any other paper except the Admit Card to the examination hall.
No candidate will be allowed to leave the examination hall before expiry or the prescribed time of the paper.
The use of calculating devices including logarithm-table, calculator or electronic gadgets such as mobile phone is not allowed inside the examination hall.
Candidates must abide by the instructions given by the Supervisor / Invigilator. If any candidate is found obstructing the work of invigilator, his/her candidature will be summarily cancelled.

A candidate found in possession of any incriminating articles or materials such as reading materials, books, notes and any electronic gadgets such as mobile phones, ear buds, Bluetooth devices, pen-camera, button-hole camera, scanner and so on, whether in use or not, will be deemed to have been using unfair means and is liable to penal action as deemed fit, including cancellation of candidature and debarment from future examinations conducted by the Central Government for a period of three years.

Candidates should bring a photo-bearing identity proof in original, such as Voter ID, Passport, Driving License, PAN Card or Aadhaar Card, failing which they will not be allowed to appear in the examination.

content_sections.heading: DGQA Technician Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: The DGQA Technician eligibility conditions cover nationality, qualification, age, service-related conditions, disqualifications and medical fitness. Candidates should read each condition carefully because the notification sets specific requirements for each post and category. Only Indian nationals are eligible to apply. No person is eligible for appointment who: has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, provided that the Government may exempt any person from this rule if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal law applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for doing so; or is convicted or under trial for associating with criminal offences. Candidates must be in good mental and physical health and free from any physical deformity that may interfere with the efficient discharge of duties. Provisionally shortlisted candidates will have to undergo a medical examination prescribed by the Competent Authority (Government Hospital) before an offer of appointment is issued. A candidate found unfit will not be offered an appointment. Candidates diagnosed with night blindness or colour blindness, as determined by the prescribed medical authority, will be declared medically unfit for appointment to the post. They will not be considered for selection or offered appointment, irrespective of their performance at any stage of the recruitment process. The decision of the designated Medical Board / Medical Officer regarding such visual defects is final and binding. Candidature in a reserved category remains provisional until the veracity of the supporting documents is ascertained by the authority. Candidates belonging to SC/ST/EWS/OBC/PwBD must enclose the latest copy of the caste certificate or other relevant certificate issued by a Competent Authority. The benefit of reservation under EWS is applicable upon production of an Income and Asset Certificate as per Annexure - IV issued by a Competent Authority. The notification names the following as authorities who can issue the caste certificate: Chief Metropolitan Magistrate / Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate / Metropolitan Magistrate. Revenue Officer not below the rank of Tehsildar and Sub-Divisional Officer of the area where the candidate and his/her family resides. District Magistrate / Additional District Magistrate / Collector / Deputy Collector / Commissioner / Deputy Commissioner / Additional Deputy Commissioner / First Class Stipendiary Magistrate / Sub Divisional Magistrate / Taluka Magistrate / Executive Magistrate / Extra Assistant Commissioner (not below the rank of First Class Stipendiary Magistrate). Central Government civilian employees claiming age relaxation must hold a certificate in the prescribed format (Annexure - I) from their office, showing continuous service of not less than three years

content_sections.heading: DGQA Technician Selection Process
content_sections.text: The selection process has two stages: a Written Test and a Trade Test. A merit list is then prepared, and final appointment depends on document verification, medical examination and verification of character and antecedents. Eligible candidates have to appear in the Written Test, which will be conducted in one session, either in the forenoon or afternoon of the day. The test is of objective type with multiple choice questions only. There is no negative marking for wrong answers. The examination will be conducted in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh. The exact date, time and venue will be mentioned in the Admit Card. The question papers will be as per the syllabus in Tenth Standard / Matriculation of Central / State Boards. The question paper is in three parts. Part (i) is in English and Hindi; Parts (ii) and (iii) are in English only. Candidates are shortlisted after the Written Test based on marks obtained and the category of reservation. Candidates shortlisted on the basis of the Written Test will be called for the Trade Test. The names of shortlisted candidates will be published either on the same day or the next day of the Written Test, and the Trade Test will be conducted after shortlisting. After the Written Test and Trade Test, a merit list is prepared on the basis of marks obtained. If more than one candidate secures equal marks (trade-cum-station wise), the tie is resolved in the following sequence: Date of birth, with the older candidate placed higher. Candidate with higher marks in Numerical Aptitude. Candidate with higher marks in English Language and Comprehension. Selected candidates will be informed of their provisional selection after completion of the selection process, and no correspondence in this regard will be entertained before that. Success in the Written Test and Trade Test confers no right of appointment unless the Government is satisfied, after such enquiry as may be considered necessary, that the candidate is suitable in all respects for the service or post. The appointment letter will be strictly based on the veracity of the documents submitted with the application, including supporting documents for eligibility criteria and the reserved category certificate (not applicable for UR candidates), as well as the Medical Examination Report, Verification of Character and Antecedents, and any other requirement mentioned in the application and specified by the Government of India.

content_sections.text: Apply only online at apssb.nic.in between 21 October (3:00 PM) and 5 November 2026 (5:00 PM). Applications by any other mode are rejected. Upload: scanned signature on white paper in black ink (10–50 KB, JPG/JPEG/PNG); recent passport-size photograph (50–100 KB, JPG/JPEG/PNG); and copies of the educational and technical certificates relevant to the posts applied for. content_sections.heading: TNPSC Group 4 Photo and Signature Size 2026
content_sections.text: Candidates applying for the TNPSC Group 4 Notification 2026 must upload their photograph and signature in the size, dimensions and format prescribed by TNPSC. Incorrect, unclear or improperly sized images may result in problems while submitting the online application. The photograph uploaded for the TNPSC Group 4 2026 application should be a recent colour passport-size photograph taken in a photo studio against a white background . The candidate should face the camera directly, with both ears and part of the neck clearly visible. The photograph should measure 3.5 cm in width and 4.5 cm in height (130 × 170 pixels) . The image file should be between 20 KB and 50 KB , scanned at 200 DPI and saved in JPG format. The candidate's name and the date on which the photograph was taken should be printed at the bottom of the photograph. For this recruitment, the photograph should have been taken on or after 06 October 2026 , the date of the TNPSC Group 4 notification. Of the total 4.5 cm photograph height, the candidate's image should occupy approximately 3.0 cm (115 pixels) , while the name and date portion should occupy approximately 1.5 cm (55 pixels) . For the signature image, draw a box measuring 6.0 cm × 2.0 cm on a white sheet and sign inside the box using a blue or black ink pen . Scan the signature at 200 DPI and crop the image so that only the signature box is visible. The final signature should measure approximately 230 × 75 pixels and have a file size between 10 KB and 20 KB . Save it as a JPG image before uploading. Photo Size: 20 KB to 50 KB Photo Dimensions: 130 × 170 pixels Photo Physical Size: 3.5 cm × 4.5 cm Signature Size: 10 KB to 20 KB Signature Dimensions: 230 × 75 pixels Signature Physical Size: 6.0 cm × 2.0 cm Resolution: 200 DPI File Format: JPG Important: Avoid selfies, mobile-phone photographs, photocopied photographs or photographs with unsuitable backgrounds. Upload clear images in the prescribed size and format.

content_sections.heading: TNPSC Group 4 Photo Compressor – Resize Photo and Signature Online
content_sections.text: If your TNPSC Group 4 photograph or signature is larger than the prescribed upload size, you can resize and compress the image before submitting the application. Use the TNPSC Group 4 Photo Compressor and Image Resizer to adjust the photograph or signature to the required dimensions and file size. For the TNPSC Group 4 application, resize the photograph to 130 × 170 pixels and 20 KB–50 KB . The signature should be resized to 230 × 75 pixels and 10 KB–20 KB . Open the FreeJobAlert Image Resizer . Upload your TNPSC Group 4 passport-size photograph. Set the required dimensions to 130 × 170 pixels . Keep the final file size between 20 KB and 50 KB . Download the resized image and check that your face, name and photograph date are clearly visible. Upload the final JPG image while filling the TNPSC Group 4 online application. Sign with blue or black ink inside a 6.0 cm × 2.0 cm box on white paper. Scan or create a clear digital image of the signature. Open the FreeJobAlert Image Resizer . Resize the signature to 230 × 75 pixels . Keep the final file size between 10 KB and 20 KB . Save the image in JPG format and upload it to the TNPSC application portal. Tip: After compressing the photograph or signature, open the downloaded image once and make sure it is clear and not blurred before uploading it to the TNPSC portal.

content_sections.heading: NER Scouts & Guides Quota Selection Process
content_sections.text: Candidates found eligible will be assessed on the basis of a written examination (60 marks) and marks on certificates (40 marks), for a total of 100 marks. Candidates found eligible for appointment must also pass the prescribed medical examination conducted by the Railway administration. Separate Computer Based Tests (CBT) will be conducted for Level-2 (Group 'C') and Level-1 (erstwhile Group 'D') posts. The paper consists of 40 objective type questions (40 marks) and 01 essay type question (20 marks) relating to the Scouts and Guides organization and its activities and General Knowledge, as per the syllabus. 01 mark is awarded for each correct answer and 1/3 mark is deducted for every incorrect answer. There is no negative marking for the essay type question. The minimum qualifying marks in the written examination for all candidates are 40%. Based on written examination performance, candidates equal to 5 times the number of vacancies will be called for Document Verification, separately for Level-2 and Level-1 posts. Empanelment will be made in order of merit, prepared according to the overall marks obtained in the Written Examination and Marks on Certificates. The notification lists the following topics: History of Scouting/Guiding; Law and promise; Organisation – 'District & State level'; Training Center – 'District and State level'; Knowledge of Books; Scouting for Boys/Guiding for Girls in India; Motto; Left handshake; Salute; Prayer; Flag song; National Anthem; Know the National and Scouting Flags; Social services at various occasions; Hiking; Proficiency Badges, How these are earned?; Stages in Scouting/Guiding; Thinking Day; Progressive Training of Scouts/Guides/Rovers/Rangers; Pioneering; Handicrafts; Indian Railway Jamborette; National Jamboree; Jamboree On the Air; Organisation at National Level; National training Centers, WAGGGS/WOSM – Uprashtrapati Award Competition; Prime Minister Shield Competition; Community Development Programs; Aims and Methods of Scouting; How Scouting is useful in producing better citizens?

Fill in the online application form with accurate details, as no corrections are allowed after final submission.

Upload a recent passport size colour photograph (JPG/JPEG, 4 KB to 100 KB, between 100 x 100 and 300 x 350 pixels) with a white or light background, face occupying about 50% of the area, without sunglasses, scarf or cap.

Upload your signature (JPG/JPEG, 2 KB to 50 KB, between 100 x 50 and 200 x 200 pixels), signed on white paper with a black ink pen in running hand. Blurred photographs or signatures lead to rejection.

Only a single online application has to be submitted. The selection process involves a single-stage Computer Based Test (CBT) and Aptitude Test (wherever applicable)
followed by Document Verification and Medical Examination. Selection is made strictly on merit based on these stages. The date
time and venue of all activities will be fixed by RRC and intimated to eligible candidates in due course. Requests for postponement or change of venue
date and shift will not be entertained under any circumstances.

The CBT has questions and answer options only in English and Hindi. There is negative marking in the CBTs for all categories of posts: 1/3rd of the marks allotted for each question is deducted for each wrong answer. There is no supplementary exam for absentee candidates under any circumstances. Candidates absent on the scheduled date and session will be disqualified without further notice. The syllabus and examination pattern are the same as prescribed by RRB for Direct Recruitment
except the ALP category
for which a revised pattern is given in Annexure-A (as per RBE 28/2026 dated 23.03.2026).
The subject-wise distribution is indicative
and question papers may vary. There will be a separate CBT for each pay level of Technician posts. A virtual calculator is available on the computer monitor during the JE CBT.
ALP: Mathematics
General Intelligence and Reasoning

and Basic Science and Engineering follow the RRB Direct Recruitment syllabus for ALP. The Trade Specific Section is based on the syllabus prescribed by the Directorate General of Training (DGT) under MSDE for the relevant trades
available at www.dgt.gov.in. Technician Gr-I S&T: General Awareness
Basics of Computers and Applications
Mathematics
and Basic Science and Engineering (including Electricity and Magnetism
and Electronics and Measurements). Technician Gr-III: Mathematics
and General Science (Physics
Chemistry and Life Sciences of 10th standard level) with General Awareness. Junior Engineer: General Awareness
Physics and Chemistry (up to 10th standard CBSE syllabus)
Basics of Environment and Pollution Control
and Technical Abilities framed on the syllabus of the chosen Exam Group (Civil and Allied
Electrical and Allied
Electronics and Allied
or Mechanical and Allied Engineering). NTPC (Non-Graduate): Mathematics
and General Awareness.

The topic-wise syllabus for each group is given in Annexures A to D of the official notification and is not reproduced in full here. The topics listed in the notification are illustrative and not necessarily exhaustive.
Candidates equal to 8 (eight) times the number of ALP vacancies for each notified community/category (UR
OBC (NCL)
SC
ST) are shortlisted for CBAT based on CBT marks. If more than one candidate obtains marks equal to the cut-off
all of them are shortlisted. Each test battery/section of CBAT must be cleared separately. All candidates
irrespective of community
must secure a minimum T-score of 42 in each test battery separately
with no relaxation. CBAT is only in English and Hindi
with no negative marking. The merit list is prepared only from candidates qualifying in CBAT
with 50% weightage to CBT marks and 50% weightage to CBAT score (Railway Board's letter no. 2023/E(RRB)/25/38-A dated 16.04.2026). For CBAT information
the notification refers candidates to the RDSO website (rdso.indianrailways.gov.in).
The CBTST is of qualifying nature

and its marks are not added for merit. Candidates equal to eight times the number of vacancies for each community are called. Candidates should be able to type 30 words per minute (WPM) in English or 25 WPM in Hindi on a Personal Computer without editing tools and spell check. Kruti Dev and Mangal fonts are available for Hindi typing. Exemption may be extended to candidates permanently disabled due to Blindness/Low Vision
Cerebral Palsy and Locomotor Disability with not less than 40% permanent disability
who must upload or produce the Typing Skill Test Exemption Certificate issued by the Competent Medical Board before the test.

These percentages may be relaxed by 2% for PwBD candidates if there is a shortage of PwBD candidates against the vacancies reserved for them. The marks scored in CBT are used for shortlisting candidates for further stages. Candidates equal to the number of vacancies are called for Document Verification
based on merit in CBT and the preference for post/exam group given. Tie-break: the older candidate is placed higher in merit; if the age is also the same

alphabetical order (A to Z) of the name is used. Normalization: raw marks are used for single-session papers and normalized marks for multi-session papers to compute a Merit Index. Merit Index = Sq + (St − Sq) × (M − Mq) / (Mt − Mq)
where M is the marks obtained
Mq is the qualifying marks for the general category candidate (40)
Mt is the mean marks of the top 0.1% or top 10 candidates (whichever is larger)
Sq is 350 (score assigned to Mq) and St is 900 (score assigned to Mt). A combined merit list of candidates from different disciplines/Exam Groups is prepared in descending order of the Merit Index
and allotment of preference is done on that basis. Post/Unit is allotted as per the candidate's options
subject to merit
reservation policy and vacancy position on the date of finalizing the panel. Once empanelled
candidates forfeit the right to be considered for any other post/category.

syllabus.details: ALP: Mathematics, General Intelligence and Reasoning, and Basic Science and Engineering follow the RRB Direct Recruitment syllabus for ALP. The Trade Specific Section is based on the syllabus prescribed by the Directorate General of Training (DGT) under MSDE for the relevant trades, available at www.dgt.gov.in. Technician Gr-I S&T: General Awareness, General Intelligence and Reasoning, Basics of Computers and Applications, Mathematics, and Basic Science and Engineering (including Electricity and Magnetism, and Electronics and Measurements). Technician Gr-III: Mathematics, General Intelligence and Reasoning, and General Science (Physics, Chemistry and Life Sciences of 10th standard level) with General Awareness. Junior Engineer: General Awareness, Physics and Chemistry (up to 10th standard CBSE syllabus), Basics of Computers and Applications, Basics of Environment and Pollution Control, and Technical Abilities framed on the syllabus of the chosen Exam Group (Civil and Allied, Electrical and Allied, Electronics and Allied, or Mechanical and Allied Engineering). NTPC (Non-Graduate): Mathematics, General Intelligence and Reasoning, and General Awareness. | The topic-wise syllabus for each group is given in Annexures A to D of the official notification and is not reproduced in full here. The topics listed in the notification are illustrative and not necessarily exhaustive.

how_to_apply: Visit the official website of RRC/NCR, www.rrcpryj.org, and open the link for filling the application for GDCE Notification No. RRC/NCR/GDCE/01/2026.
Click on the "New Registration" link.
Fill in the personal information, e-mail address and mobile number. An e-mail/SMS will be received on the registered e-mail ID/mobile number with the registration number and password.
Login using the registration number and password.
Follow the instructions and complete the registration process step by step, including the post preference and exam group.
Upload the scanned copy of the photograph, self-attested certificates in proof of date of birth, educational/technical qualifications and caste certificate (SC/ST/OBC), and submit the application.

Name, Father's Name and Date of Birth must match the Matriculation or equivalent certificate as well as the service records. Candidates need not send printouts of the application or certificates to RRC by post.
Proof of Date of Birth, and disability certificate for PwBD.
Certificate of Educational/Technical Qualification for the post applied.
For SC/ST candidates: Community certificate in the prescribed format as per Annexure-G.

For OBC candidates: valid Community certificate in the prescribed format as per Annexure-H, specifically indicating that the candidate does not belong to the creamy layer, plus the self-declaration as per Annexure-H (1).

Employee Service Certificate as per Annexure-I, filled by the applicant with signature and thumb impression (same as uploaded in the application) and verified by the immediate supervisor with signature, seal and mobile number.
Passport size colour photograph and specimen signature, in JPEG format.
The application also asks for Division/PU, Community, Employee ID No., Aadhar No., two visible marks of identification, and nearest Railway Station and Station Code.
important_instructions: Applications are to be submitted online only through the link on www.rrcpryj.org. Candidates are advised to beware of fake websites and job racketeers. RRC does not appoint any agent or coaching centre for recruitment. Candidates must have their own valid and active mobile number and personal e-mail ID for the entire examination process. RRC will not entertain any request to change the mobile number or e-mail ID after submission of the application. Candidates should register well before the closing date to avoid last-minute load on the website. RRC will not bear responsibility if a candidate cannot register within the last date and time. Post preference, once opted, is treated as final and no change is permissible. Candidates with partial options are considered only for the posts/categories they opted for. Not giving an option for certain posts/categories is treated as unwillingness for them. Eligibility is considered only on the basis of information furnished in the online application. False or incorrect information or suppression of relevant information leads to rejection of candidature. Candidates should note and preserve their Registration Number for further stages. Signatures and photographs must be identical at all stages of the selection process. Candidates should keep at least 12 copies of the same photograph. Candidates must ensure they meet the medical standards for the post. Appointment is subject to medical fitness, final verification of educational and community certificates, and verification of antecedents/character. Selected employees are liable to be posted anywhere in North Central Railway, and the decision of the Railway administration is final. Selection by RRC does not confer any right of appointment. RRC only recommends names to the concerned units of North Central Railway, which issue the offer of appointment letter.
Applications are liable to be rejected on grounds including the following (the list is illustrative and not exhaustive):

Applications sent manually and not registered online. More than one application by the same candidate for the same post. Candidates submitting multiple applications, including with minor changes in information, will be summarily rejected and debarred from all future examinations of RRBs and RRCs. Not possessing the prescribed educational qualifications at the time of submitting the application. Missing or improper scanned photograph, signature, LTI and other documents. Invalid photographs (black and white, with cap or sunglasses/goggles, disfigured, small size, full body, one-side view, unrecognizable, photostat copy, group photo, selfie, photo taken by mobile, morphed photo, or no photo). Signature in capital/block/disjointed letters. Missing certificates in the prescribed format for date of birth, educational qualification and caste. Incomplete or incorrectly filled applications.
If an application is rejected, candidates can view the status and reasons online on www.rrcpryj.org, and SMS/e-mail alerts are also sent. The decision is final and binding.

E-Call Letters are to be downloaded from the official website of RRC. No call letter is sent by post. For the CBT, candidates must bring their Railway Identity card and a sparing letter (with the candidate's photo) bearing the signature and stamp of the concerned Supervisor/Controlling Officer, with the photo attested. Name, date of birth and photo on the ID must match the online application. Candidates must bring the colour photograph (35 mm x 45 mm) uploaded with the application, and an original valid Photo ID. Candidates must write the Self-Declaration paragraph, sign and affix LTI at the venue in the presence of the invigilator only. Writing it in advance or signing in capital letters leads to rejection. Banned items inside the exam hall include mobile phones, Bluetooth devices, pen drives, laptops, calculators, wrist/smart watches, other communication devices, pen/pencil, wallets/purses, belts, shoes and metallic wear including ornaments. For Document Verification, candidates must bring all required documents in original, along with two sets of self-attested photocopies. Certificates must be in English or Hindi in the prescribed formats. Candidates absent during Document Verification will have their candidature cancelled. Candidates who want to be considered against reserved vacancies or seek age relaxation must submit the relevant original certificate in the prescribed format at Document Verification; otherwise they will be considered under General (UR) if eligible.

Any candidate using unfair means, sending someone else in their place or attempting to impersonate will be debarred from all examinations of all RRCs and RRBs for lifetime, in addition to departmental disciplinary action and possible legal prosecution. The notification refers to The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act and Rules, 2024, as amended on 31.07.2026. RRC may conduct post-examination analysis including log analysis, photograph and biometric verification and CCTV footage review.

content_sections.heading: RRC NCR GDCE Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: Eligible and serving regular employees (except RPF/RPSF) having lien in North Central Railway can apply against the GDCE quota. All eligible regular and serving railway employees of NCR can fill the online application form. No minimum service condition is prescribed, as per RBE 72/2024 dated 02.08.2024. Regular and eligible NCR employees who have the prescribed educational qualification for Direct Recruitment and work in grades lower than the grade/pay scale for which GDCE is being conducted can appear for all categories. Regular and eligible employees with the prescribed educational qualification for Direct Recruitment who work in the same grade/pay scale for which GDCE is being conducted can appear for selection from Non-Safety to Safety category posts as well as Safety to Safety category posts. Candidates must fulfil all notified eligibility criteria on or before the closing date for submission of the application. Date of Birth and educational qualifications must be updated in the Service Records and in HRMS; otherwise the application is liable to be cancelled. Employees in a higher grade than the grade of the notified post. Employees who do not have the requisite educational qualification, medical standard and age criteria prescribed in the notification. Trainee or Substitute employees who are not regularized. RPF/RPSF personnel (as per Railway Board's letter No. E(NG)I/2002/PM2/9 dated 11.08.2003). Law Assistant, Catering Inspector and Accounts Cadre (as per Railway Board's letter No. E(NG)I/2000/PN2/12 dated 21.08.2001, RBE No. 165/2001). Candidates appearing in, or awaiting results of, the final examination for the minimum qualification at the time of applying. Candidates who have resigned or been transferred from North Central Railway at any stage of the selection process. Candidates are not allowed to apply for the same post on which they are presently working.

content_sections.heading: RRC NCR GDCE Qualification
content_sections.text: Candidates must hold the minimum educational qualification for the post from a recognized Board/ University/ Institute as on the closing date for online application submission, as per Annexure-F. The qualification must also be endorsed in the Service Record of the employee, otherwise the candidature will be rejected. Those awaiting results of the final examination of the prescribed qualification should not apply. Qualification notes from the notification: for JE and ALP posts, higher qualifications such as B.E./B.Tech are also acceptable in lieu of a three-year Diploma in Engineering in the same disciplines. Diploma/Degree in Engineering will not be accepted in lieu of Course Completed Act Apprentices/ITI for the post of Technicians in Pay Level-2 unless otherwise specified, and a Graduate Act Apprentice will not be accepted in lieu of Course Completed Act Apprenticeship (CCAA), as per RBE 13/2019 dated 16/01/2019. Please note: Annexure-F groups the JE qualifications in merged cells, and it lists ten JE rows, while Annexure-E lists eleven JE categories (for example JE / Drawing (Electrical), JE / TMC and JE (Mech.) do not appear by the same names in Annexure-F). Candidates should check the exact qualification for their post in Annexure-F of the official notification. Candidates must indicate the ITI trade from which they wish to appear in the Qualifying Test for ALP and Technician posts, and the Exam Group for the "Technical Abilities" part of the JE examination. For ALP, candidates holding a Degree/Diploma select the relevant trade against their engineering discipline as shown below. A candidate holding more than one minimum educational qualification mapped to different Exam Groups can choose any one Exam Group, provided the candidate opts for post(s) whose educational qualification is mapped to the chosen exam group. Such candidates would still be eligible for all the opted posts as per educational qualification.

content_sections.heading: RRC NCR GDCE Age Limit
content_sections.text: The upper age limit for UR candidates is 42 years, for OBC candidates 45 years and for SC/ST candidates 47 years. The lower and upper age limits are reckoned as on 01.01.2027 (both dates inclusive). The lower limit is 18 years for all communities/categories. Note on a discrepancy in the notification: the age-group table in the notification labels the OBC column as "18 to 47 Years", while clause 2.1 and the OBC date of birth (02.01.1982) point to an upper limit of 45 years. The table above follows clause 2.1 and the date of birth; candidates should confirm this with the official notification. No age relaxation is allowed to SC/ST/OBC-NCL (Non-Creamy Layer) candidates applying against unreserved vacancies. Proof of age: any one of the Birth Certificate issued by the competent authority, OR the Class 10th (or equivalent) Certificate/Mark Sheet indicating the date of birth, OR the School Leaving Certificate clearly mentioning the date of birth, and the same recorded in the service record of the employee. Candidates should ensure that they meet the prescribed age limit as on the specified cut-off date. You can use our Age Calculator to check your exact age and confirm your eligibility before applying.

content_sections.heading: RRC NCR GDCE Reservation
content_sections.text: Vertical reservation for SC, ST and OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) is admissible wherever applicable. SC/ST candidates must furnish a Caste Certificate in the format at Annexure-G, and OBC-NCL candidates in the format at Annexure-H, at the time of Document Verification. OBC-NCL candidates must also furnish a declaration in the format at Annexure-H (1) that they do not belong to the creamy layer. The certificate should not be older than one year at the time of Document Verification. If these stipulations are not complied with, the OBC-NCL claim will not be entertained and the candidate, if otherwise fulfilling the General (UR) conditions, will be considered under General (UR) vacancies only. There is no separate reservation of posts for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS), as per Railway Board's letter No. E(NG)I-2018/PM1/23 dated 02/05/2019 (RBE No. 72/2019). The crucial date for the claim of SC/ST/OBC status or any other benefit such as reservation and age relaxation, where not specified otherwise, is the closing date for submission of online applications. Reservation for PwBD is a horizontal reservation and is applicable in GDCE, as per Railway Board's letter No. E(NG)1-2019/PM4/8 dated 27.12.2022.

content_sections.heading: RRC NCR GDCE Salary
content_sections.text: The notification does not specify the salary or pay amount for the posts. It gives only the 7th CPC pay level of each post. During any prescribed training, payment will be regulated as per extant rules. The medical standards are indicative and not exhaustive. Candidates should read Chapter 5 of the Indian Railway Medical Manual (IRMM) Volume I, which can be accessed at www.indianrailway.gov.in. A candidate who fails to pass the prescribed medical fitness for the post will not be considered suitable for empanelment. Annexure-F shows the suitability of each post for persons with benchmark disabilities. The table below lists the entries as given in the notification. "No" means the post is not marked suitable for that disability category. Abbreviations as given in the notification: AAV = Acid Attack Victim, B = Blind, BL = Both Legs, D = Deaf, DW = Dwarfism, HH = Hard of Hearing, HI = Hearing Impairment, ID = Intellectual Disability, LC = Leprosy Cured, LD = Locomotor Disability, LV = Low Vision, MD = Multiple Disability, MW = Muscular Weakness, OA = One Arm, OL = One Leg, OAL = One Arm and One Leg, PwBD = Persons with Benchmark Disabilities, VI = Visually Impairment. SD and SI are used in the notification without an expansion. Selected PwBD candidates will be medically examined by Railway Medical Authorities at the time of Document Verification, and only those conforming to the medical standards in the Indian Railway Medical Manual and other extant provisions will be eligible for appointment.

content_sections.heading: RRC NCR GDCE Selection Process
content_sections.text: Only a single online application has to be submitted. The selection process involves a single-stage Computer Based Test (CBT) and Aptitude Test (wherever applicable), followed by Document Verification and Medical Examination. Selection is made strictly on merit based on these stages. The date, time and venue of all activities will be fixed by RRC and intimated to eligible candidates in due course. Requests for postponement or change of venue, date and shift will not be entertained under any circumstances. The CBT has questions and answer options only in English and Hindi. There is negative marking in the CBTs for all categories of posts: 1/3rd of the marks allotted for each question is deducted for each wrong answer. There is no supplementary exam for absentee candidates under any circumstances. Candidates absent on the scheduled date and session will be disqualified without further notice. The syllabus and examination pattern are the same as prescribed by RRB for Direct Recruitment, except the ALP category, for which a revised pattern is given in Annexure-A (as per RBE 28/2026 dated 23.03.2026). The subject-wise distribution is indicative, and question papers may vary. There will be a separate CBT for each pay level of Technician posts. A virtual calculator is available on the computer monitor during the JE CBT. ALP: Mathematics, General Intelligence and Reasoning, and Basic Science and Engineering follow the RRB Direct Recruitment syllabus for ALP. The Trade Specific Section is based on the syllabus prescribed by the Directorate General of Training (DGT) under MSDE for the relevant trades, available at www.dgt.gov.in. Technician Gr-I S&T: General Awareness, General Intelligence and Reasoning, Basics of Computers and Applications, Mathematics, and Basic Science and Engineering (including Electricity and Magnetism, and Electronics and Measurements). Technician Gr-III: Mathematics, General Intelligence and Reasoning, and General Science (Physics, Chemistry and Life Sciences of 10th standard level) with General Awareness. Junior Engineer: General Awareness, Physics and Chemistry (up to 10th standard CBSE syllabus), Basics of Computers and Applications, Basics of Environment and Pollution Control, and Technical Abilities framed on the syllabus of the chosen Exam Group (Civil and Allied, Electrical and Allied, Electronics and Allied, or Mechanical and Allied Engineering). NTPC (Non-Graduate): Mathematics, General Intelligence and Reasoning, and General Awareness. The topic-wise syllabus for each group is given in Annexures A to D of the official notification and is not reproduced in full here. The topics listed in the notification are illustrative and not necessarily exhaustive. Candidates equal to 8 (eight) times the number of ALP vacancies for each notified community/category (UR, OBC (NCL), SC, ST) are shortlisted for CBAT based on CBT marks. If more than one candidate obtains marks equal to the cut-off, all of them are shortlisted. Each test batt

content_sections.heading: RRC How to Apply for NCR GDCE Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Visit the official website of RRC/NCR, www.rrcpryj.org, and open the link for filling the application for GDCE Notification No. RRC/NCR/GDCE/01/2026. Click on the "New Registration" link. Fill in the personal information, e-mail address and mobile number. An e-mail/SMS will be received on the registered e-mail ID/mobile number with the registration number and password. Login using the registration number and password. Follow the instructions and complete the registration process step by step, including the post preference and exam group. Upload the scanned copy of the photograph, self-attested certificates in proof of date of birth, educational/technical qualifications and caste certificate (SC/ST/OBC), and submit the application. Name, Father's Name and Date of Birth must match the Matriculation or equivalent certificate as well as the service records. Candidates need not send printouts of the application or certificates to RRC by post. Proof of Date of Birth, and disability certificate for PwBD. Certificate of Educational/Technical Qualification for the post applied. For SC/ST candidates: Community certificate in the prescribed format as per Annexure-G. For OBC candidates: valid Community certificate in the prescribed format as per Annexure-H, specifically indicating that the candidate does not belong to the creamy layer, plus the self-declaration as per Annexure-H (1). Employee Service Certificate as per Annexure-I, filled by the applicant with signature and thumb impression (same as uploaded in the application) and verified by the immediate supervisor with signature, seal and mobile number. Passport size colour photograph and specimen signature, in JPEG format. The application also asks for Division/PU, Community, Employee ID No., Aadhar No., two visible marks of identification, and nearest Railway Station and Station Code.

content_sections.heading: RRC NCR GDCE Important Instructions for Candidates
content_sections.text: Applications are to be submitted online only through the link on www.rrcpryj.org. Candidates are advised to beware of fake websites and job racketeers. RRC does not appoint any agent or coaching centre for recruitment. Candidates must have their own valid and active mobile number and personal e-mail ID for the entire examination process. RRC will not entertain any request to change the mobile number or e-mail ID after submission of the application. Candidates should register well before the closing date to avoid last-minute load on the website. RRC will not bear responsibility if a candidate cannot register within the last date and time. Post preference, once opted, is treated as final and no change is permissible. Candidates with partial options are considered only for the posts/categories they opted for. Not giving an option for certain posts/categories is treated as unwillingness for them. Eligibility is considered only on the basis of information furnished in the online application. False or incorrect information or suppression of relevant information leads to rejection of candidature. Candidates should note and preserve their Registration Number for further stages. Signatures and photographs must be identical at all stages of the selection process. Candidates should keep at least 12 copies of the same photograph. Candidates must ensure they meet the medical standards for the post. Appointment is subject to medical fitness, final verification of educational and community certificates, and verification of antecedents/character. Selected employees are liable to be posted anywhere in North Central Railway, and the decision of the Railway administration is final. Selection by RRC does not confer any right of appointment. RRC only recommends names to the concerned units of North Central Railway, which issue the offer of appointment letter. Applications are liable to be rejected on grounds including the following (the list is illustrative and not exhaustive): Applications sent manually and not registered online. More than one application by the same candidate for the same post. Candidates submitting multiple applications, including with minor changes in information, will be summarily rejected and debarred from all future examinations of RRBs and RRCs. Not possessing the prescribed educational qualifications at the time of submitting the application. Missing or improper scanned photograph, signature, LTI and other documents. Invalid photographs (black and white, with cap or sunglasses/goggles, disfigured, small size, full body, one-side view, unrecognizable, photostat copy, group photo, selfie, photo taken by mobile, morphed photo, or no photo). Signature in capital/block/disjointed letters. Missing certificates in the prescribed format for date of birth, educational qualification and caste. Incomplete or incorrectly filled applications. If an application is rejected, candidates can view the status and reasons online on www.rrcpryj.org, and SMS/e-ma

faq.question: Q1. What is NCR GDCE Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: NCR GDCE Recruitment 2026 is the General Departmental Competitive Examination recruitment notified by the Railway Recruitment Cell, North Central Railway, Prayagraj, under Notification No. RRC/NCR/GDCE - 01/2026 dated 28.09.2026. faq.question: Q2. How many vacancies are available in NCR GDCE 2026?
faq.answer: The post-wise vacancies in Annexure-E add up to 656: 428 for Assistant Loco Pilot, 61 for Technician posts, 60 for Junior Engineer posts and 107 for NTPC (Non-Graduate) posts. The notification does not state a separate grand total, and the vacancies are provisional.

faq.answer: The last date is 30.10.2026 at 23:59 hrs. Online applications open on 01.10.2026.

faq.answer: Only eligible serving regular employees (except RPF/RPSF) having lien in North Central Railway can apply. No minimum service condition is prescribed as per RBE 72/2024 dated 02.08.2024. Outside candidates cannot apply under this notification.

faq.question: Q5. What is the qualification for NCR GDCE 2026?
faq.answer: It depends on the post. ALP and Technician posts require Matriculation/SSLC plus ITI or Course Completed Act Apprenticeship in specified trades (with Diploma or Degree options for ALP and Technician-I, and 10+2 with Physics and Maths as an option for Technician-III Sig & Tele). faq.answer: The lower age limit is 18 years for all categories. The upper age limit is 42 years for UR, 45 years for OBC and 47 years for SC/ST, reckoned as on 01.01.2027.

faq.answer: The selection process has a single-stage CBT, followed by an Aptitude Test for ALP (CBAT) or a Typing Skill Test for Junior Clerk cum Typist (CBTST), Document Verification and Medical Examination. Selection is strictly on merit.

faq.question: Q9. What is the salary for NCR GDCE 2026 posts?
faq.answer: The salary amount is not specified in the notification. The posts fall under 7th CPC Pay Levels 2 (ALP, Technician-III, Junior Clerk cum Typist), 3 (Commercial cum Ticket Clerk), 5 (Technician-I) and 6 (Junior Engineer).

content_sections.heading: APPSC Various Posts Selection Process
content_sections.text: As stated in each of the notifications, selection for all 8 posts will be through a single-level examination only - no Screening Test will be conducted, irrespective of the number of applications received. The examination will be conducted in online Computer-Based Recruitment Test (CBRT) mode. Where the single-level examination is held in multiple sessions, the Commission will apply a normalisation process to the marks, wherever considered necessary and applicable, as per a methodology to be notified by the Commission in due course. For the Executive Officer Grade-III post, the notification additionally specifies the following examination scheme (as per Annexure-V of G.O.Ms.No.201, Finance (HR-I Plg. & Policy) Dept., dated 21/12/2017): For this post, each wrong answer is penalised with 1/3rd of the marks prescribed for that question, as per G.O.Ms. No.235, Finance (HR-I, Plg & Policy) Dept., dated 06/12/2016. The detailed scheme and syllabus for each post's examination is annexed to its respective notification; candidates should refer to the specific notification for their post to see the complete subject-wise syllabus.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for APPSC Various Posts Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Applications must be submitted online only, through the Commission's website psc.ap.gov.in , between 16 October 2026 and 5 November 2026 (up to 11:59 PM). Applications submitted through any mode other than the prescribed online mode will not be entertained under any circumstances. Candidates should read the Commission's Detailed Notification and other instructions carefully before applying, and enter their particulars correctly in the online application form. Candidates are advised to submit their applications well in advance of the last date to avoid last-minute rush.

content_sections.heading: APPSC Various Posts Important Instructions
content_sections.text: Applicants must satisfy themselves regarding the terms and conditions of the respective Recruitment Notification before applying online. The number of vacancies notified is provisional and subject to variation upon confirmation from the concerned department. Applicants must possess the requisite educational qualification as on the date of the Detailed Notification, not the date of the Brief Notification. The Detailed Notification carrying the full breakup of vacancies, scale of pay, age, community-wise reservation, educational qualification, and other instructions will be published on the Commission's website on or before 16 October 2026. The date of the Detailed Notification will be reckoned as the crucial date in all aspects, including eligibility. For the Forest Section Officer, Forest Beat Officer, and Forest Range Officer posts, physical requirements/standards will be specified in the online Detailed Notification. The examination for each post is a single-level online (CBRT) test; no separate Screening Test will be held regardless of the number of applicants.

content_sections.heading: Selection and Interview
content_sections.text: Selection has two stages: a written examination (Stage-I, 70 marks) and then an interview/viva-voce with document verification (Stage-II, 20 marks). The written examination has objective multiple-choice questions, answered on an OMR sheet. It lasts 1½ hours (90 minutes). The Mizo language part is qualifying only. To pass the written examination, a candidate must score at least 40% in it, i.e. 8 out of 20 marks. Marks from the Mizo part are not counted when the merit list is prepared. Candidates are called for the interview/viva-voce and document verification on the basis of their written-examination merit, in the ratio of 1:3 (3 candidates for each post). To qualify, a candidate must score at least 60% in the interview, i.e. 12 out of 20 marks. Final selection is based on the total marks from the written examination and the interview/viva-voce. If two or more candidates have the same total, the one with more written-examination marks is preferred. If those marks are also equal, the older candidate is preferred. The High Court reserves the right to fix or change the cut-off marks for the written examination and the viva-voce. Selected candidates may be assigned any Group-D position(s) based on administrative convenience.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable District-wise Vacancy 2026
content_sections.text: The 1,053 regular recruitment vacancies are distributed among participating districts according to the approved tribal ratio based on the 2011 Census. The district allocation also includes separate male and female vacancies. The original notification provides detailed tribe-wise allocations within these districts in Annexure I. Applicants must check the specific tribe and district allocation before selecting their application district.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Backlog Vacancy 2026
content_sections.text: The notification also provides 84 backlog Constable GD vacancies reserved for specific tribes and districts whose vacancies remained unfilled in the preceding recruitment. All 84 backlog vacancies are allocated to male candidates. Special Condition: The single Phom backlog vacancy under Mokokchung is restricted to eligible members of the Phom tribe belonging to Anaki (Old) and Anaki 'C' villages. Candidates applying for backlog posts must satisfy the exact district, residence and tribe conditions provided in Annexure III.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Eligibility Criteria 2026
content_sections.text: The educational qualification for Nagaland Police Constable GD Recruitment 2026 depends on the applicant's tribe classification. Candidates must also possess valid documents establishing their Indigenous Inhabitant and tribal eligibility. The educational qualification must be from a recognized board or educational authority. Where a pass certificate or provisional pass certificate has not been issued, the notification requires an appropriate certificate or letter from the concerned educational institution or authority. The recruitment is open to eligible male and female candidates from Indigenous Inhabitant Tribes of Nagaland who meet the prescribed age, education, district and physical fitness requirements. Applicants must possess an Indigenous Inhabitant Certificate and relevant tribal certificates issued by the competent authority. Eligible natives or residents of Dimapur, Chumoukedima and Niuland can apply under the combined allocation for these three districts, provided they possess the prescribed supporting certificates. The notification also provides specific arrangements for members of the Chang, Sumi and Phom tribes from identified villages in Mokokchung, Wokha and Shamator districts. Candidates affected by these provisions should refer to the detailed conditions in the official notification.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Age Limit 2026
content_sections.text: Serving Government employees may receive upper-age relaxation equivalent to their qualifying service, subject to a maximum of five years and the applicable Government policy. The notification also provides age-relaxation conditions for certain incumbent Nagaland Police Constables and petitioners covered by the specified Gauhati High Court judgments and orders.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Salary 2026
content_sections.text: The advertised Constable GD posts carry Pay Level 3, with Grade Pay Rs. 1,800 under the specified pay-band structure of Rs. 5,200–20,200.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Application Fee 2026
content_sections.text: The examination fee for Nagaland Police Constable Recruitment 2026 is Rs. 300 . Applicants must pay the fee online as part of the application process.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Selection Process 2026
content_sections.text: Selection for the Constable GD posts involves physical and medical screening, outdoor physical efficiency tests, an objective-type written examination, interview and NCC certification assessment. Candidates must qualify in the required physical and medical standards before participating in outdoor tests. Only candidates who qualify the PET will be called for the written examination.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Physical Standard Test 2026
content_sections.text: The notification prescribes different minimum height and chest measurements for male and female candidates. Candidates who do not meet the physical requirements may be disqualified during the recruitment process.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Physical Efficiency Test 2026
content_sections.text: The Physical Efficiency Test carries 45 marks and includes running, pull-ups, high jump and long jump. Male and female candidates have separate qualifying standards. Disqualification: Male candidates taking longer than 12 minutes 30 seconds and female candidates taking longer than 12 minutes will be disqualified. Nagaland Police Constable Syllabus 2026 Male candidates completing fewer than six pull-ups and female candidates completing fewer than three pull-ups will be disqualified. A maximum of three attempts is permitted. Candidates who fail to meet the required qualifying standard in any of the outdoor tests will not be permitted to continue in the recruitment process.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Written Exam Pattern 2026
content_sections.text: The Nagaland Police Constable written examination will consist of 80 multiple-choice questions carrying 40 marks. Candidates will receive two hours to complete the question paper, which will be set in English.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Written Exam Syllabus 2026
content_sections.text: The written examination may cover the following subjects and knowledge areas specified in the official notification: General Awareness and General Knowledge General Science Indian History Indian Polity Social Sciences Elementary Mathematics Sports Naga Culture and Heritage Nagaland State and Naga Tribes General Mental Aptitude

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Interview and NCC Marks 2026
content_sections.text: After the PET and written examination, candidates will be shortlisted for interview based on the aggregate marks obtained in these two stages. The shortlisting ratio is three candidates for each available post. The interview carries 10 marks, and NCC certification may contribute up to 5 additional marks to the overall merit assessment.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Medical Fitness Requirements
content_sections.text: Candidates must satisfy the medical fitness standards prescribed for police service. Medical examination includes assessment of height, weight, chest, vision, hearing and physical fitness. The notification identifies several disqualifying conditions, including: Eyesight below the prescribed standard. Colour blindness. Deafness or serious hearing impairment. Varicose veins. Squint eyes. Amputated limbs or physical extremities. Physical deformities, including flat feet and knocked knees. Adverse drug screening or alcohol abuse test findings. Candidates must also satisfy the medical and physical requirements during the recruitment process and subsequent training.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply Online for Nagaland Police Constable Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Eligible applicants must submit their applications through the Nagaland Police Registration Portal between 31 October and 30 November 2026. Offline applications will not be accepted. Important: Applicants must submit only through the official online recruitment portal. Applications submitted to police offices or other establishments will not be accepted.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Documents Required 2026
content_sections.text: Original documents must be produced whenever required during the recruitment process. Applicants should ensure that the details submitted online match their supporting certificates.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Probation and Posting
content_sections.text: Selected candidates will undergo a probation period of two years. Service confirmation will depend on satisfactory completion of probation, medical clearance and verification of antecedents under the applicable rules. Fresh recruits will initially be deployed in India Reserve (IR) Battalions and may be required to serve within or outside Nagaland according to the instructions of the Nagaland Police Department.
